## Bring up a new machine

1. Install Node **22.12+** (a supported even-numbered LTS release is appropriate).
2. Make pnpm **11.22.0** available. If it is absent, use `npx --yes pnpm@11.22.0` as the launcher for the commands below; npm here bootstraps pnpm, it does not install the app dependencies.
3. From the project root:

```sh
pnpm --version
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm build
pnpm dev
```

If pnpm is not installed globally:

```sh
npx --yes pnpm@11.22.0 install --frozen-lockfile
npx --yes pnpm@11.22.0 test
npx --yes pnpm@11.22.0 build
npx --yes pnpm@11.22.0 dev
```

Read the URL Vite prints; it normally uses port 5173 but may select another if occupied. No absolute filesystem paths, OS-specific shell commands, global pnpm install, or old running processes are required.

### Google Maps setup

Create `.env.local` from `.env.example` and set:

```dotenv
VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=your_browser_key
```

Vite also reads `.env`; `.env.local` overrides a conflicting `.env` value. `.env.example` is documentation only. Restart Vite after configuring the key. Both real environment files are ignored by Git.

Enable Maps JavaScript API and billing. Restrict the browser key to this API and the relevant HTTP referrers. `http://localhost:5173/*` and `http://127.0.0.1:5173/*` are different referrers; allow whichever you use, plus the deployed site. A browser key is public in the client bundle by design. Never use a secret OpenAI key in a `VITE_*` variable.

The first machine has a user-provided `.env`; its value is deliberately not in this handoff. The app now starts in **Marina 3D**, using local generated assets regardless of key presence. The key is only needed for the separate live Street View mode or recapturing sources. Source images are processed locally; no image-generation API is used.

## Architecture and extension points

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/App.tsx` | Selected location/mode, game session state, overall UI, information dialogs. Keys `StreetView` by location to reset viewpoint state. |
| `src/data/locations.ts` | Four destinations and three approximate panorama search points each. Edit starting positions/headings here. |
| `src/components/StreetView.tsx` | Official panorama viewer; 200 m outdoor nearest search; viewpoint tabs; look/move/recenter controls; status/errors; listener cleanup. |
| `src/lib/google-maps.ts` | Shared browser SDK Promise, async callback loader, timeout/network/auth reporting. |
| `src/lib/street-view-navigation.ts` | Selects a forward/backward connected panorama by heading, handling north wraparound and dead ends. |
| `src/game/World.tsx` | Procedural Three.js world; requestAnimationFrame loop; camera movement; click raycasting; resource disposal. |
| `src/game/physics.ts` | Speed limits, acceleration/braking, and checkpoint count. |
| `src/styles.css` | Responsive styling, including dedicated Street View frame and controls. |
| `src/components/MarinaWorld.tsx` | Loads estimated-depth meshes; walk/drive, mouse look, touch controls, reset, bounded exploration. Shows an explicit missing-assets status until reconstruction is built. |
| `scripts/capture-marina.mjs` | Budgeted, cached four-image capture. Reads the local key without logging it. |
| `scripts/api-budget.mjs` | Reserves attempts before network access, persistent 1,000-attempt cap, and local capture lock. |
| `scripts/reconstruct-marina.mjs`, `scripts/depth-mesh.mjs` | Local ONNX depth inference and approximate textured geometry export. |
| `reconstruction/api-usage.json` | Persistent request ledger; include when transferring work. |
| `src/**/*.test.ts` | Eleven current unit tests, run through Vitest. |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Dependency cooldown and esbuild-only build-script allowance. |

Historical scaffold state was in React/in-memory refs. The current app adds the local armory save and FPS/collision described above; there is still no database, authentication, backend or multiplayer. External services are Google Maps and Google Fonts, plus a model-weight download for the local reconstruction build. Authorized captures and derived scene assets now exist. The browser loads only generated assets in Marina 3D; the model runs offline at build time. See the reconstruction README for limitations.

## Fast manual acceptance check

1. Reload: Marina 3D should load the waterfront scene without requiring a key or making a Static API request. Click the canvas, use WASD, drag to look, switch Walk/Drive, and reset. The gold ring marks the exploration limit; distances are approximate.
2. For the optional live viewer, choose Street View and try destinations/tabs. This uses the configured key and separate Maps JavaScript traffic.
3. In that viewer, turn left/right, step along the road, and recenter. Step buttons may be disabled if no connected photograph exists in the current direction. Rotate to find a path.
4. Switch to Joyride: start, hold W/up, steer with A/D, brake with S/Space, pause/resume/reset, and complete all three gates.
5. Switch to Target practice: hit all five orange targets and reset.
6. Test a narrow/mobile viewport. Ensure the Google attribution is not obscured and the app does not overflow horizontally.
7. With no key, confirm the no-key demo still works. If testing an invalid key, never print it in logs or commit it.

## Known limits and next steps

- The small four-image Marina proof of concept now works. Next validate depth at more viewing angles and decide whether to extend with translated captures, calibrated geometry/scale, and actual collision. Do not silently spend more image quota. The current asset format is JSON BufferGeometry plus JPEG, not GLB.
- Image generation is optional for texture/appearance completion. Its output does not replace geometry, camera calibration, collision, or validation of spatial consistency. No GPT-Image-2.5 endpoint/access has been verified; use the actual event-provided capability rather than inventing a model/API contract.
- A Google Maps warning was recorded before the final key update. Static API now works; the auxiliary live viewer should be rechecked separately if used in a demo. Preserve source attribution and capture date in the reconstruction.
- Approximate search points are not guaranteed landmark coordinates; Google may snap multiple points to the same panorama. Human curation of heading and distinctness remains useful.
- Street View transitions between capture positions. Do not add fabricated speed/distance claims or imply it supplies depth/collision geometry.
- Test slow networks, failed authorization, unavailable imagery, and rapid viewpoint switching more deeply. The SDK is shared within a page; after changing key restrictions or an authorization failure, a full reload is the reliable recovery path.
- The generic 3D scene varies palette/height, not neighborhood geography. Improving it requires original or suitably licensed data/assets.
- Terms/privacy dialogs are prototype text; keyboard focus trapping and an accessibility pass remain open.
- Highest-value next step: evaluate and improve the bounded depth reconstruction before expanding capture volume. Do not make further panorama navigation the main deliverable. See `.agents/PLAN.md` for acceptance criteria and ordered work.

## Deploy on a new host

Static frontend: install `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, build `pnpm build`, publish `dist`. Configure the Maps key at **build time**, add the deployed referrer to the key, and rebuild after env changes. No SPA path rewrites are currently needed because there are no pathname routes.

Before finishing a change, run relevant tests and `pnpm build`, record what you actually verified in `.agents/PLAN.md`, and update this handoff if setup or architecture changes. Do not claim that a local test proves the public deployment works.

## 2026-10-24: optic reflections every frame, paid for by a lighter pass

Follow-up to 3b0b5f2. weapon-reflections.ts now captures every frame at the
hip as well as aimed, and the per-capture cost dropped from ~64 to ~19 draw
calls in the Marina range (WebGL draw-call count per framebuffer, swiftshader),
so it is cheaper than the old 20/s hip schedule (~21 draws/frame averaged).

  (far = 150, near ≤ 65% of it) so scenery fades rather than pops, then restored.

## 2026-10-24: bullet-decal normal maps made visible again

The decal atlas already carried a normal map (02eec05), but its per-instance
strength was `(depth / radius) / (.007 / .041)`, calibrated to the old
`.041 * bore` hole radius. c630bc9 widened holes to `.075 * bore^1.5` without
touching that constant, so the issued rifle drew at 0.55 strength and the P30 at
0.18: in headless renders a concrete crater was pixel-identical with the normal
map on or off.
- `scorchRelief` (fps-impacts.ts) replaces the inline formula: square root of
  depth-to-radius over DEFAULT_IMPACT_PROFILE's, capped at 4. The issued rifle is
  1, P30 ≈ 0.57, FN MAG ≈ 1.18, CIS 50MG ≈ 1.77; blood stays 0.
- docs/ARMORY.md describes it, and its 7.62 mm width ratio is corrected to 1.6.
Validation: 1053 tests in 111 files pass, typecheck. impact-materials fixture rendered in
headless Chrome (swiftshader), normalScale 1 vs 0, fixture sun and a raking
light: concrete rims and walls, wood fibres, metal dimples and the glass pit now
shade visibly. Not done: glass crack lines and blood have no relief of their own
(the crack painter's height is only the central pit).

## 2026-10-24: interruptible, resumable reloads (STALKER 2's "reload renewal")

- fps-rules: rounds now go in at a commit point (`reloadCommit`: .74 tactical,
  the end of MAG IN; .9 from empty, after CHAMBER) instead of at the end.
  `interruptReload` stops a reload: before the commit it is `suspended`
  (magazine untouched, progress kept in `WeaponState.reloadSaved`), after it
  `finished`. `beginReload` resumes from `reloadSaved`, clamped short of the
  commit. `reloadEmpty` is now on the state.
- fps-reload: the input gate. A fresh trigger pull (with rounds in the gun) or
  a fresh sprint interrupts; inputs held when the reload began do not, and a
  held sprint drops to a run until the reload ends.
- fps-engine: interrupts on fire/sprint (on foot), weapon switch and vehicle
  entry (both used to throw the progress away). HUD `reloadSaved` drives
  `R RESUME RELOAD · n%`; the magazine digits climb only through MAG IN and
  land at the commit point (`magazineDisplay(..., start, commit)`).
- arena-rules (host): same commit point, `startReload`/`stopReload` with
  resume, a reloading:true→false input stops the reload, weapon switch and
  vehicle seat suspend it. RELOAD_COMMIT_GRACE (.12) lets a guest that stopped
  just after its own commit keep the fresh magazine. arena-runtime marks shot
  inputs `reloading: false`, so an interrupt-and-fire is not refused.
Validation: unit tests for the rules, gate, HUD climb and host mirror; full
suite and typecheck. In headless Chromium (scene runs ~1 fps on swiftshader, so
the page's rAF clock was slowed 12x): fire during MAG OUT suspended at 25%, the
old magazine fired 26→24, the HUD showed the resume prompt, and R resumed in
MAG OUT and landed 30 at SEAT MAG. scripts/fps-handling-smoke.mjs gained an
interrupt/resume step but fails before it here at the existing sustained-fire
spread check, on the unmodified code too. Not done: a +1 chambered round on
tactical reloads, quick items interrupting, single-round (shotgun) reloads.

## 2026-10-24: the chamber and an empty magazine well

- fps-rules: `magazine` is every round in the gun, the chambered one included.
  `WeaponSpec.bolt` ('open' on Ultimax, FN MAG, CIS 50MG, MG4; closed
  otherwise). Closed bolt: `chambered` round, full load capacity + 1
  (`fullLoad`), fires the chambered round with the magazine out. Open bolt:
  `chambered` means cocked; never a round in the chamber; runs home dry.
  Helpers `chamberRound`, `magazineRounds`, `roundReady`, `canReload`.
- Reload points (`RELOAD_POINTS`): out .38 (removed magazine's rounds back to
  the reserve, `magazineOut`), seat .74, chamber .9 on an empty reload (an empty
  reload clears `chambered` first). Commit stays seat/chamber. A suspended
  reload can leave an empty well (`magazineOut`) or a seated, unchambered
  magazine; `canReload` covers both even with no reserve.
- arena-rules host now keeps `ammo: WeaponState[]` and calls the same
  fps-rules functions with an unlimited reserve (ArenaWeapon gained `bolt`).
- HUD: digits are the magazine; `+1` badge for a chambered round; prompts
  NO MAGAZINE / CHAMBER EMPTY. Pilot observation reports 0 rounds when nothing
  is ready to fire. Checkpoint restore clamps to `fullLoad`.
Validation: 1065 tests in 112 files, typecheck. Headless Chromium (slowed rAF clock):
26+1 → R → 00+1 at MAG OUT → fire at MAG IN fired only the chambered round,
"NO MAGAZINE · R RESUME RELOAD · 55%" → R resumed as an empty reload from MAG
IN and ended 29+1. A one-frame 30+1 at the chamber step was fixed in
magazineDisplay.

## 2026-10-25: district map, hit directions, timed supplies, time of day, bots that heal

- Map: M (or tapping the minimap on touch) toggles `hud.mapExpanded`;

- Hit directions (`fps-hit-direction.ts`): arena hits record `hurtFrom
  { x, z, serial, blast? }` on the victim (shooter, vehicle gun origin or
  blast point); counter-fire uses the firing target. The engine owns a pooled
  DOM overlay of arcs re-bearinged every frame; same-direction hits merge.
- Supplies (`fps-healing.ts`, `fps-supply-viewmodel.ts`): G and expedition
  medical crates start a timed use (eat / bandage / medkit / plates / ammo) with
  a commit point; fresh fire or sprint (the reload gate), R, weapon switch,
  vehicle or death stop it before anything is spent. Weapon lowered, walk at
  0.55×, no aim. Medical crates are collected only at commit.
- Lighting (`world-lighting.ts`): Singapore sun path, keyed by elevation to key
  colour/scale, fill scale and colours, sky tint and exposure; moon as key at
  night. `EnvironmentSettings` gained `timeOfDay` ('auto' = Singapore clock)
  and `shadows`. `world-atmosphere` moves and recolours each district's own sun
  and sky (`atmosphere.light` reports the result). Daytime fill is ~0.58× the
  authored hemisphere, which is most of the "less flat" change. FPS sun shadows
  (`fps-sun-shadows.ts`): 2048² PCF-soft map, ±64 m, following the camera,
  texel-snapped, shadowMap.autoUpdate off with one update a frame; skipped on
  SwiftShader/llvmpipe. The weapon's view lights follow the same hour.
- Bots (`arena-bot-combat.ts`): a spawn's loadout slot is the drawn variant's
  `variantSpec`; host shots by bots use `hitDamage` (falloff + head precision
  via `headHit`). Bursts by role (`burst`), cadence from the weapon's interval,

  out of sight they kneel (eye 1.15) and dress for 3.2 s for +55%; a hit
  interrupts; snapshot `healing` drives `CharacterDrive.healing` on the rig.
  Role shotDelay values were re-tuned as pauses between bursts.

## 2026-10-25: sky light and ambient occlusion

- Sky light (`world-sky-light.ts`): given the renderer, `createWorldAtmosphere`
  hides the district's hemisphere light and lights the scene from a 128×64 sky
  image (PMREM, rebuilt at most every 0.3 s when the quantised light changes):
  bluer zenith, paler horizon, glow round the key, and ground lit by the actual
  sun for bounce. Scaled so walls average what the hemisphere gave them, so
  shade is redistributed between faces rather than brightened;
  `scene.environmentIntensity` = hemisphere intensity / π each frame. Glass and
  other Standard/Physical surfaces now also reflect the sky.
- Ambient occlusion (`world-occlusion.ts`): three's GTAO at half resolution
  from the scene pass's own depth (normals from depth, no second scene draw),
  over a 4× MSAA half-float target, then OutputPass for tone mapping. A colour
  sky is cleared on the canvas, not tone-mapped. r180's GTAOPass constructor
  breaks if given a depth texture, so `setGBuffer` is called after. Skipped on
  software renderers. New `occlusion` setting (default on) with a World
  conditions toggle; FPS, region and Marina views all use it.
Validation: `world-sky-light.test.ts`, the settings test, full suite and
typecheck; `pnpm test:fps:field-kit` passes (one earlier run failed the
dressing-health check while counter-fire kept landing; the rerun passed).
Not done: frame cost not measured on real hardware; no cascaded shadows for
distant towers; AO does not reach the weapon viewmodel.

## 2026-10-25: touch trigger buffer, stance beside the left stick

- Tap-to-fire was unreliable on phones: the engine samples `trigger` once a
  frame, so a tap released before the next frame (slow phones run 20–30 fps) or
  landing inside the last round's cooldown never fired. `pullTrigger` in
  `fps-engine.ts` now buffers a fresh press for `TRIGGER_BUFFER` (.18 s); the
  buffer is cleared when a round leaves, on reload/supply start, weapon switch
  and `clearInput`. Mouse fire shares the same path. A buffered pull also counts
  as a fresh pull for reload/supply interruption and arena vehicle fire.

## 2026-10-25: faction heat that moves, and a friendly side that shows up

- Friendly heat sat at 0–0.05: the forces' band floors were 0–0.1, their
  troops ran `[0, 4]`, so a district at rest wanted no friendly soldiers, and
  enemy losses only leaked them about 0.05 that drained in seconds. A
  10-minute soak in Marina Bay and Raffles Place with the player killing a
  contractor every 15 s saw no friendly rides and no kills between the factions.
  Contractor heat barely moved either, because each kill's bump drained in about 35 s.
- `faction-heat.ts`: new `DISTRICT_HEAT` bands (forces rest at 0.1–0.15,
  below the contractors), forces troops `[1, 6]` and top-up `[60, 20]` s.
  A casualty holds heat 30 s (a smaller rise its share of that), then decay
  runs 0.5×–2× by how high the side is. The last stretch of a band climbs
  slower. Non-lethal hits add `contact`. District strength is pulled halfway
  to the hottest sector. New `surge`/`surgeAt` (0 at floor, 1 at ceiling).
- `arena-rules.ts`: hits feed heat; bot-only fights count for `skirmish`
  (0.25); top-up rides read heat when checked (`state.last` instead of a
  fixed `topUp`); home leash grows to 2× with surge; the director gets
  `tempo` from both sides' surge (`HEAT_PACE`).
- `combat-director.ts`: `tempo` divides the wait and is re-read each step.
  `refused` now clears the drawn gap too, so a retry comes 5 s later.
- `fps-engine.ts`: `HEAT_CALLS` radio lines (Intel/HQ) as the hottest sector
  crosses steps; arriving in a district only takes a reading.
- Soak after the change (same harness, open ground): idle, both sides rest
  near their floors with occasional squad skirmishes. Fighting takes both
  sides to their ceilings within about 2 minutes, with 40+ kills between the
  factions in 10 minutes and about 12 rides per side. After the player
  leaves, both sides are back at rest within 3–4 minutes.
Validation: full suite, typecheck; Marina Bay in the browser pane (touch
mode) with no console errors, where the HUD forces bar read 29% and rose to
its 65% ceiling as the player took fire. The radio lines were not seen on
screen: the comms log is hidden in the touch layout. Not soak-tested on real

## 2026-10-25: bot aim that settles, a spawn shield, and bot ranks

Players were dying in two or three hits in the open world. Bots fire their
variant's full damage (kept), but they also tracked perfectly with hitscan:
64–100% of rounds landed on a standing player, and strafing changed nothing.
- Aim (`BOT_AIM`, `botAimScale` in arena-bot-combat): error opens at 4× on
  first sight and settles over 1.6 s, the settled error is 1.5× the role's
  `spread`, a moving target adds 15% per m/s (a sprint about doubles it), and a
  moving bot adds up to 50%. Losing sight resets it. Target speed is measured
  per member in `step()` (`speed`, smoothed).
- Turns: at most `BOT_AIM.shooters` (2) bots fire on one player at a time
  (`takeTurn`); the others hold fire and keep moving. Bot-vs-bot is unlimited.
- `SPAWN_SHIELD_SECONDS` (3): bots hold fire on (and do not start aiming at) a
  freshly spawned player; the player's first shot ends it. Bullets only.
- Ranks (`arena-ranks.ts`): recruit / regular / veteran, drawn at every spawn
  from `rankMix(strength)` (heat; half strength without it). Rank scales aim
  (1.4 / 1 / .75), reaction (+.25 / 0 / −.15 s), armour (.6 / 1 / 1.4, then
  heat), dressings (+1 veteran) and reweights `chooseArmament` by catalog tier.
  Names are the rank's title plus a callsign (Black Kite: Recruit / Operator /
  Veteran; forces: Pte / Cpl / Sgt, no longer by role). `ArenaActor.rank` is
  the grade; avatars rebuild when rank or name changes. Event crews keep their
  names but are ranked.
- Looks: right sleeve shows 1–3 chevrons (`chevrons` patch design); recruits
  are faded with no plates, pack or shades; veterans wear plates, a pack and
  shades, Black Kite veterans a helmet. Labels draw chevrons before the name
  (`paintNameLabel`). Fixture: `scripts/fixtures/bot-ranks.html`.
Measured (one bot, open ground, settled): assault hits a standing player
31 / 46 / 59% by rank, a walking one 23 / 38 / 42%; four assault bots kill an
unplated player standing in the open about 2–5 s after the shield drops.
Validation: full vitest, typecheck; rank figures and labels checked in the
browser pane. Not played in a live district (mouse capture is blocked in the
pane). Not done: no HUD cue for the shield, and garrison bots join the feed
under their bare callsign (the rank title comes with the first spawn).

## 2026-10-25: every carried gun's rounds travel, on the arena host too

Every base weapon was `HITSCAN`; only three elite variants flew, and only on the
Training range, because the arena host resolved every shot instantly.
- `muzzleBallistics(real m/s)` in fps-ballistics: velocity × `BALLISTIC_SCALE`
  (.55), drop 9.8. Rifles ≈ 506–534 m/s, MGs 462–509, P30 198; the three elite
  barrels 578–638 (Fort Siloso had been slower than issue). Table in
  docs/ARMORY.md.
- Arena host: `shoot` → `launch` queues an `ArenaRound` (walls and rendered
  cover measured once along the line); `stepRounds` at the top of `step` tests
  each tick's stretch of arc against people, vehicles and raiders through
  `resolveShot(..., flown)`, pricing falloff at the whole distance. Players'
  landed hits queue per shooter; `takeHits(id)`, `inFlight(id?)`. Capped at
  `MAX_ARENA_ROUNDS` (96). `ArenaWeapon.ballistics` is sanitized, defaulting by
  family.
- Runtime: `deliverHits` after each host step sets our hit marker and sends a
  guest `arena-hit` when its round lands (`mergeHits` folds several into one).
- Engine: in the arena the shot goes to the host with only scenery capping its
  range (a figure may step aside), and a `cosmetic` round flies locally for the
  tracer and impact.
- Bots lead moving targets by `BotRank.lead` (.3 / .6 / .85) of the flight and
  aim up for drop (`leadRay`); target velocity is tracked per member.
- Tests: `shootAndLand` (arena-test-shots.ts) fires and steps in 2 ms slices
  until the round lands; recoil tests use plain `shoot`; runtime tests advance
  the fake clock; arena-rounds.test.ts covers arrival time and dodging.
Measured: bot hit rates at 7–25 m barely moved; snipers at 50 m lose most
against movers. Validation: full vitest, typecheck, build. Not played live
(mouse capture is blocked in the browser pane). Vehicle guns and the raid
helicopter's gun still resolve instantly; bots' rounds draw no tracer.

## 2026-10-25: vehicle and raider guns fly, and everyone's rounds draw tracers

- Vehicle guns: `VEHICLE_COMBAT[kind].ballistics` (car 462 m/s, helicopter 490).
  On the arena host the gunner's shot is `send`-queued with `vehicle` set, so it

  `PublishedRound`), validated on guests. The engine adopts them each frame via

## 2026-10-25: other shooters' strikes in their own gun's look

`PublishedRound` gains `calibre` and `power`; the host fills them from the

## 2026-10-25: city lights at dusk and night

At dusk and night the districts had only the dimmed sun and moon. New
`world-night-lights.ts`, created by fps-engine next to the atmosphere:
- `placeStreetLamps` (alternate kerbs, `LAMP_SPACING` 30 m, along `mapRoads`)
  and `placePathLamps` (jittered 34 m grid over open ground no streetlamp
  reaches); both skip footprints, carriageways, the map edge, water
  (`fpsWater` boxes) and points under non-solid walk surfaces, and stand on
  solid terrain surfaces. Cosmetic: `fpsEffect`, no raycast, no colliders.
- `bakeLampMap` → one RGBA8 DataTexture (R pool light, G ground height).
  Every Standard/Lambert/Phong material in the scene gets an
  `onBeforeCompile` (chained onto any existing one; rescanned every 1.5 s for
  vehicles and people) that adds `albedo × lamp colour × pool` to emissive,
  gated by height above the pool's ground.
- Building-sized meshes (box/extrude/tower-shaped cylinder, ≥7 m tall,
  ≥4.5 m deep, not green, not transparent, not in the elevated-places
  groups) get a geometry view with a `nightSpan` attribute (per instance for
  InstancedMesh) and a cloned material with a window grid. Dispose restores
  geometry, materials and hooks.
- Heads, halos (custom-blended points), stars and moon (at infinity,
  thinned by fog distance). `nightLevel(elevation)` drives it; pools follow
  level², blackout puts it out. A viewmodel `lampLight` uses `lightAt`.
- world-atmosphere now snaps to the hour's light on the first frame instead
  of easing in from the authored daylight over ~15 s.
Validation: full vitest, typecheck, build; Marina, Chinatown and Orchard
checked at dusk and night in the browser pane (no console errors). Other
districts covered only by the unit test (every district gets >8 lamps, all
on free ground, and some windowed meshes). Frame cost not measured on a GPU.

## 2026-10-26: touch aim assist

New `aim-assist.ts` (pure maths) and `aim-assist-setting.ts` (localStorage
`blockplay-sg-aim-assist-v1`, on by default). Only a thumb's drag is
assisted (`look(dx, dy, true)` from the scene drag and the fire button's
`lookBy`); the mouse and the AI pilot never are. Inside a cone of 2.5 target
radii (clamped 1.2°–5°) the drag's away/across component loses up to 30% and
its towards component gains up to 20%, never past the target and never while
the trigger is held. With the thumb still nothing moves, so recoil climb is
untouched and pulling it back down is the player's work. The engine picks the
lock at 10 Hz (`refreshAimAssist`, one sight raycast per aim point already in
the cone, via `visiblePilotContacts` over the new shared `combatSubjects()`),
then recomputes angles from yaw/pitch on every drag; `canvas.dataset.aimAssist`
reads `locked` while one is held. Toggle: "Aim assist" on the range/expedition
start card (`FpsPlayerTools`, touch only) and the arena card.
Validation: full vitest, typecheck; headless Chromium with CDP touch on the
Marina range: drag off the target damped (0.0289 vs 0.0359 rad), off-target
and assist-off drags exact. Not tried on a real phone or in a LAN match.

## 2026-10-26: night vision and thermal devices

New armory category `vision` (shop tab "Night vision"), one device worn at a
time (`profile.vision`, default `vision-none`; restored only if owned; weight
joins `armorWeightKg`). Five devices after S.T.A.L.K.E.R.'s tiers: NV-1/2+/3
image-intensifier tubes and TI-1/TI-2 thermal cores. Picture parameters live
in `vision-devices.ts` (`VISION_DEVICES`, keyed by catalog id), with the state
machine (warm-up, TI-1's calibration freeze, palettes, the touch button's
off → on → palettes → off walk) and `visionGain` (≈1 by day, rated gain at
night or in a blackout). `fps-vision.ts`:
- NVG multiplies tone-mapping exposure by the gain before any world pass
  (scope and reflections included), then a post pass reads the finished canvas
  back (`copyFramebufferToTexture`) and draws phosphor, grain, scintillation,
  halo (quarter-res bright pass), blur, barrel distortion and the image circle
  (scaled from the screen's longer side).
- Thermal swaps every eligible mesh onto a cached unlit temperature
  ShaderMaterial (rescanned every 0.4 s, restored on switch-off/dispose unless
  game code replaced the material meanwhile). Heat comes from tags:
  `impactSurface: 'flesh'` → body, `userData.heat` 'engine' (vehicle models,
  raid truck), 'target' (range targets), 'none' (figure's `rig-weapon`).
  `fpsEffect` subtrees keep their materials unless something hot is inside;
  transparent materials keep theirs unless hot (vehicle glass goes opaque).
  Sky and fog go cold for the frame. AO is skipped while thermal is on. Post:
  sensor rows, detail enhancement, level/span, fixed-pattern noise, palettes.
- Engine: H toggles, J palette, `pressVision` for touch; `hud.vision`;
  checkpoint carries `vision` across gateways; a click and tube whine.
UI: `FpsVisionChip` under the compass on desktop; on touch the eye button
carries the state as a badge. Smoke/gas overlay drops to 30% with thermal on.
Shop: `VisionDossier` compares against the worn device or the naked eye
(`visionFigures`), `visionModel` preview, tube-count silhouettes.
Validation: vitest (new vision-devices.test.ts), typecheck, build. In the
browser pane (375×812, touch path) Gen 1/Gen 3 at night, Gen 2 at noon,
TI-2 white-hot at night in the range and expedition (a bot read white against
the street) and ironbow at noon; shop tab at desktop. Sampled thermal levels
at night: sky .01, buildings ~.2, ground ~.4. Not seen: the desktop chip in
mouse play (pointer capture is blocked in the pane), TI-1's freeze, and frame
cost on a real GPU (the pane ran ~1.5 fps). The pane hides the page during a
screenshot, which trips the engine's visibility pause; that is the harness.

## 2026-10-26: fire beats sprint; the stick no longer cancels reloads

Firing while sprinting used to be ignored (`shoot()` waited for `!sprinting`),
which on touch meant easing the thumb off the stick's rim before FIRE did
anything. New `fps-sprint.ts` `advanceSprintBreak`: a held trigger drops a
sprint to a run, a pull out of a sprint fires after `SPRINT_OUT` (0.12 s,
inside the 0.18 s trigger buffer so taps still fire), and the sprint resumes
by itself `SPRINT_RESUME` (0.25 s) after the trigger is let go. Same rule on
desktop with Shift. The reload/supply gates now get only a held Shift as sprint
intent, so a stick at the rim (which wobbles across the threshold) never reads
as a fresh sprint and cancels a reload; on touch only the trigger or a weapon
change stops one. The stick sprint has hysteresis (`STICK_SPRINT` 0.92 on,
`STICK_SPRINT_RELEASE` 0.80 off), also used by `TouchStick`'s `data-sprint`.
Validation: unit tests for the break and the hysteresis; `touch-controls-smoke`
gained a two-finger "FIRE fires out of a sprint" step, which passed in an
emulated phone (headless Chrome, 5175) when run from a copy that skips the
earlier movement steps. The full smoke fails at those movement steps in headless
Chrome ("Lifting the thumb stops the player" drifts 0.08 m at ~5 fps on
SwiftShader; the half/full stick comparison runs into the range barrier at pace
2). Not tried on a real phone.

## 2026-10-26: other shooters heard; guns with weight

Bots and other players fired in silence. `gunfire-reports.ts` diffs each arena
figure's `shots` counter per snapshot (instant guns included; own shots and
seated figures left out, since vehicles sound through `adoptShared`), capped at
3 per figure and 6 nearest per snapshot. The range's counter-fire targets and
raid door guns are heard too.

Every gunshot (own, vehicle, others, door guns) now plays through
`gunshot-audio.ts`: a crack, a noise body, a falling-sine thump (≈150→50 Hz
rifle, to ≈40 Hz for the CIS 50) and an echo tail, sized by bore and damage,
into one tanh-saturated, compressed bus. Distance strips the crack before the
rumble and lengthens the echo; others are panned. Rendered offline in headless
Chrome: own rifle peak .07 → .53, energy under 150 Hz 2% → 31%, no clipping.
Chromium's compressor ducks the first ~100 ms after a context starts, so
measure after that. The bus output gain trims every gun at once. Not heard in
game; the pistol and rifle end up near equal loudness after compression.

## 2026-10-26: hitch pass (shader compiles, program churn, bullet rays)

Profiled in headless Chrome (ANGLE Metal on a virtual Mac GPU, dev build)
across Marina, Chinatown and Tuas. Steady play already held 60 fps; the
hitches were first-use work and garbage.
- **First-use shader compiles.** The first aim cost a 404 ms then a 267 ms
  frame, the first scoped shot 143 ms, the first burst six new programs.
  `warmShaders` in fps-engine now runs before `ready`: the scope lens gets its
  PiP map up front (`scopeRenderer.prepare`), combat-event models are built
  hidden (`combatVisuals.prewarm`, arena only), `compileAsync` runs for the
  world and viewmodel scenes on the canvas and on an offscreen target (tone
  mapping and colour space differ), and the scope and reflection targets are
  drawn into once (`warm`) so the GPU builds their pipelines. After: the
  worst in-play frame in the probe is one 33 ms frame; the cost moved to a
  ~350 ms frame on the ready card.
- **Per-frame shader-key rebuilds (12 idle, 18 scoped).** Three draws
  transparent `DoubleSide` materials in two passes and flags them changed for
  each: `forceSinglePass` on the effect pools, scope lens, optic glass, enemy
  reflex tint, objective beam, searchlights and danger rings (all flat or
  additive, so one pass looks the same). Materials shared by an InstancedMesh
  and plain meshes flipped program on every alternation:
  `separateInstancedMaterials` (instanced-materials.ts) gives instanced users
  a copy, before night lights patch anything. Instanced shadow casters get
  their own depth material (fps-sun-shadows). Now 0 per frame; sampled
  allocation 265 → 184 MB per 5.5 s of walking and firing (most of the rest
  is React's dev-only JSX).
- **Bullet rays.** Three tests every instance of an InstancedMesh per ray;
  districts have meshes of 400–4,300 instances. `accelerateInstancedRaycasts`
  (instanced-raycast.ts) puts a BVH over instance boxes on static instanced
  meshes ≥ 32 instances (29 in Marina; canvas `data-raycast-trees`), pruned
  by the ray's near/far; hits are identical to three's (test compares 400
  rays). Ray time per 1.2 s burst: Marina 64 → 7 ms, Chinatown 63 → 15,
  Tuas 37 → 13.
Not done: HUD `publish()` still re-renders the whole FpsGame tree 10×/s;
the forced `updateMatrixWorld(true)` calls remain; night/day shadow toggles
still recompile every material; vision devices not warmed. Validation: unit
tests (new: instanced-raycast, instanced-materials), typecheck, headless
probe, scoped screenshot. Browser smokes not run; not tried on a phone or
Windows GPU.

get them, inside the world's own `animate(time)`: pure functions of the

Queenstown's train (now named `queenstown-train`; its old 6 m/s loop is gone)
keeps a timetable: in from alternate ends, brake to EW19, door chimes, 28 s
dwell, out. Punggol's LRT shuttles station ↔ viaduct end. HarbourFront's two

(trolley, ropes, spreader; drop heights probed below the boom); the liner
sounds its horn. Tuas's flare burns. Changi alternates arrivals and departures
along x = 420, off the coast, nav lights at night. The Woodlands shuttle comes

National Day–style five-jet flypast with red and white smoke crosses every
7 min by day. Macaques sit and hop between perches at Upper Thomson (lakeside
platform railings, kopitiam roof) and Bukit Timah (station roof and platform).
Night comes from the atmosphere root's `timeOfDay`. All of it sits under a
ray-proof `fpsEffect` group and adds no colliders; set pieces start at their
time-0 places (an airliner at the origin skewed Changi's cover test).
`RegionWorld.cues(from, to)` feeds chimes, horns and aircraft roars to the

## 2026-10-27: lit windows no longer z-fight

Night windows are drawn in the building's own shader, so wherever two surfaces
shared a plane over a lit wall, depth could not order them and the panes
flickered. Three causes, three fixes in `world-night-lights.ts` and the scenes:
pitched roof slabs (Chinatown's temple, Raffles, Tampines) passed as
building-sized and got windows on their tipped ends; now only `upright` meshes
(one axis plumb, so stood-up extrusions still count) get them. The window grid,
which panes are lit and each wall's occupancy now follow the wall's plane in the
world rather than the mesh, rows anchored at world height and only whole storeys
drawn, so two buildings sharing a wall plane light the same panes; `nightSpan`
is now a vec2. Flush geometry nudged 0.1–0.2 m: Bishan's slab cores, Chinatown's
temple roof tiers (spans 58.4 - 2·tier, missing the hall's 54 m), Changi's
terminal visors, Tampines Hub's front and back bars. New test: no lit wall shares
its plane with another box face over more than 1 m² in any district (fails on
the old Tampines and Bishan). New fixture `scripts/fixtures/night-district.html
?region=&cam=&look=` renders any district at night with the game's camera range.
Validation: tests, typecheck, night screenshots of each fixed spot. Not fixed:
sub-square-metre slivers where a strip's end meets a lit wall (Punggol, Geylang,
Toa Payoh), and authored panels 0.1–0.15 m proud of lit walls (Queenstown,
Geylang, Orchard), which still fight past ~370 m where 24-bit depth at a 0.08 m
near plane runs out.

the ground (crate, supply drop, fallen soldier) carries only its magazine;
its rounds are a separate `kind: 'ammo'` pickup with `caliberMm` set beside
it (crate weapons: `beside` = crate id, full issued reserve, placed on clear
ground; bodies half the reserve, always, replacing the friendly-only 60%
pouch and `FALLEN_AMMO`; supply drops: weapon, its rounds, medical, replacing
the double generic kit). Loose ammo crates roll a calibre on their own seed
stream (55/20/15/10), amount `ammoAmount × scale`. Field ammo no longer goes

carried gun that fires it (in hand first, cap 999); with none, the card is

engine: same variant already carried adds a magazine to its reserve; a new

phantom start-of-run reserve). The card shows calibre in the type line and a
note ("Magazine loaded · keeps your 240 × 5.56 mm"). The pilot's waypoints
and reach skip loot it cannot take. Ammo cans are drawn as olive cans with a
brass band (link calibres larger). The shop's SAF pouch is unchanged.

## 2026-10-28: shared ammunition reserves by calibre

Carried weapons of the same resolved calibre now share one loose-ammo pool
(`ammo-pools.ts`), while magazines, chambers and reload progress stay per gun.
Starting reserves and rig bonuses combine only for slotted weapons; stored guns
contribute nothing. The existing weapon rules operate on numeric reserve
accessors backed by shared pools, so magazine removal, interrupted reloads and
seating conserve rounds. Pickups, duplicate weapons, ammo pouches and supply
crates top up those pools; returning a magazine can exceed the pickup cap
without a later top-up discarding rounds. Weapon swaps retain any calibre still
carried and bring only the new gun's loaded magazine.

Travel checkpoints save each pool once, restore the shared links, retain chamber
and interrupted-magazine state, and merge older independent reserves. Live
encumbrance weighs each shared reserve once plus every loaded gun. The Armory
shows calibre totals, carry instructions explain sharing, and pickup cards/HUD
reserve tooltips name the pool.

Validation: all 1,518 tests across 156 files pass (four workers, 30-second default
timeout; district diagnostics have their own longer timeout). Typecheck and
production build pass. New `pnpm test:fps:ammo` browser smoke passed through the
real engine and weapon HUD: rifle/support firing and reloading, separate
magazines, an ammo pouch spent once, HUD reserve, and reset to the starting pool.
Used the bundled Node runtime because Homebrew Node's simdjson dependency is
broken locally. Existing unrelated workspace edits were preserved.

## 2026-10-28: vision switching animations; sun flare, haze dust and lens rain

Vision devices now animate on and off (`vision-devices.ts` `mount`/`fading`,
shaders in `fps-vision.ts`). The body swings down from the top of the view
(0.28 s) with the world visible round it and powers only once lowered, so the
tube's gain and the thermal material swap wait for it. NVG lights centre-out
with a brightness surge; thermal boots with a flat field, a top-down scan and a
shutter flash. Off, the post pass holds the last frame: NVG phosphor afterglow
(per-device `shutdown`), thermal folds to a line and a point; then it swings up.
The post passes now draw premultiplied over the canvas. Reduced motion skips the
swing and fade.

occlusion read off the frame (sky = cleared background colour, eased in a 1×1
target), haze dust in three angular depth layers with parallax and forward
scattering, and simulated raindrops (land, merge, run, leave beads, dry under
shelter or in vehicles) drawn as instanced quads that refract the frame. The
atmosphere exposes eased `air` (rain, haze, sunlight, wind, sheltered).

## 2026-10-30: expedition facility warfare

Implemented independent allied/Black Kite command posts, garages and helipads
across all 19 expedition districts. Local infantry advantage advances explicit
capture/build/repair work even with remaining defenders; equal presence stalls
it, and sustained enemy advantage at the equipment suppresses deployment.
Equipment takes real bullet/blast damage. Capture preserves health, destruction
stops production, and paid reconstruction/repair restores it. Supplies belong
to each faction's district operation, separate from the permanent armory.

Operational posts deploy bounded four-soldier waves; garages/helipads gate and
charge fleet replacements. Losing every post enables slower transports through
a small set of authored outer anchors; arbitrary 45-second respawns are disabled.
Bots have stable small squad identities and shared facility objectives, including
autonomous takeover, spaced approach positions and replacement leadership.
Existing player orders override movement. Vehicle crews approach squad objectives
and dismount nearby. These are basic objective squads, not full formation AI.

Facilities and fleet health/positions survive district travel during one
expedition. Work is canceled/refunded on return; vehicle seats clear and infantry
is re-established from posts/reserves. Unloaded districts do not simulate, and
new expeditions start fresh. Motor pool placement uses the district's fixed spawn
so arrivals cannot move facilities; equipment avoids gateways, arrivals and NPCs.
Landmark buildings remain intact. There is no territory-wide capture meter or
campaign victory system. See docs/FACILITIES.md.

## 2026-10-30: navigable moonlight with geometry-based shelter

Defined comfortable as normal walking/navigation with readable nearby road
edges, kerbs and obstacles, plus exposed silhouettes; fine detail and people
in shade should remain difficult unaided. Restored clear-night moonlight and
sky fill to 0.24 each, kept exposure at 1.05 and used a muted brighter sky fill.
Cloud/rain reduce sky fill as well as direct moonlight. Water body brightness
now follows available natural light rather than a fixed nighttime percentage.

Added night-exposure.ts: a static oriented-box BVH bakes sky/moon visibility
at nine heights. Lit materials attenuate natural diffuse/specular light while
local lamps, windows, torches and flashes retain their illumination. Foliage
transmits partial light; effects, invisible meshes and water are not blockers.
Weapon lighting and water reflections use the local visibility. This works
with GPU shadows/AO disabled. The coarse field is static geometry, not dynamic
triangle shadows. Moon-channel updates are bounded to 2,048 samples per frame
and uploaded atomically, avoiding periodic full-bake frame stalls.

Fixed controller recreation binding stale uniforms in cached material programs;
night/day round trips now restore unchanged daylight. Noiseless NVG review
mode also suppresses zero-noise scintillation. All 33 focused tests and

## 2026-10-30: NV-compatible aiming lights

Lowered, powered intensifiers now activate a shared aiming profile. Visible
laser spots use a stronger neutral tube response at their original hit point
and size, then receive the actual tube's phosphor, blur and halo; the beam stays
restrained. Fitted red dots, holographic rings and canted dots use a controlled
NV core with 78% less broad optical scatter. Both canted/primary sights update
before rendering; magnified etchings stay unchanged. Raising, switching off,
thermal and bare-eye views restore ordinary illumination. This adds no separate
IR mode or new player controls, and changes no aiming/spread rules.

The GPU fixture exposed a Three r180 texture-state edge case: when the NV frame
was already cached on texture unit 0 while glow left unit 1 active, a framebuffer
copy could target the smaller glow texture, raise INVALID_VALUE and retain an
old picture. Explicitly activate unit 0 through renderer.state before each live
copy; held afterglow/calibration frames still deliberately keep their image.

Added scripts/fixtures/nv-aiming.html and scripts/fps-nv-aiming-smoke.mjs to check
real optics, rail effects and intensifier passes. All three tubes pass visible
cores, reduced dot scatter, brighter laser spots, unchanged bare-eye frames,
mount/power/thermal gating and repeated error-free framebuffer refreshes.
Unit checks cover shared live shader uniforms, canted dots and preserved scope
etching. Initial full suite: 1,828 tests/188 suites passed; final repeat after the
texture-state fix, production build/typecheck, actual-engine check and manual
release verification follow. Evidence: .cache/nv-aiming/ and

## 2026-10-30 — shootable reinforcement transports and raider bounties

Reinforcement trucks (800 HP) and helicopters (1,000 HP) now have host-owned
hulls and a real 100 HP driver/pilot actor, visible through cockpit glazing.
The hull and driver have separate hitboxes; rays stop at the first hull/body or
world surface. Friendly small-arms fire is harmless; world blasts can damage
hulls. At <=25% hull health, a truck stops or a helicopter descends at 5 m/s;
half the remaining passengers attempt to leave, rounded down. A driver/pilot
kill releases all remaining passengers, including after a partial evacuation.
Helicopter occupants wait for touchdown. Exits retry when blocked/occupied;
passengers leave every .7 s and run clear for up to 3 s before resuming combat.
Destruction kills the driver, cancels booked inserts, removes undelivered
recruits and restarts fallen regulars' waiting clocks. Escaped troops remain
vulnerable to the shared cover-aware blast. Air wrecks fall; smoke, fire,
scorched paint, stopped rotors and HUD/audio follow live state. Departure,
reset and bounded event cleanup release driver actors and passenger bookings.
The hulls remain scripted transports, separate from the drivable fleet.

Raid helicopter shoot-downs pay 100 credits / 125 XP; drone shoot-downs pay
40 credits / 50 XP. A validated host feed bounty credits the final shooter
once through the existing profile ledger and both FPS/expedition callbacks.
It appears in the HUD and contributes to callouts, without adding an infantry
kill to match scoring. Destruction notices alone no longer pay an infantry
reward. Withdrawal, drone self-detonation and uncredited outcomes pay nothing.

## 2026-10-30: continuous cinematic deployment and mission briefing

## 2026-10-30 — range drills and equipment resupply

Added Classic, Continuous and a 90-second challenge to every district's practice
range, independently of Practice / Counter-fire. The seeded director reuses the
eight authored target slots, keeps up to three appearing/active targets, assigns
unique activation IDs, raises/retracts targets and cools each position for 2–5 s.
New appearances avoid positions within 4 m of the player. Maps and pilot subjects
track current activations, and clearing a target cancels its pending counter-fire.
Retracted targets release their movement collider. Changing drill reuses the
loaded renderer/assets; reset and pause preserve the intended clock semantics.
Continuous and early-ended timed drills keep elimination rewards without a
completion bonus; a finished timed challenge and Classic validate their own
finish rules rather than a universal count of eight. Tutorial/arena/expedition
rules remain separate. Waves and moving targets are deferred.

Every field range has a labelled equipment box near the start, with a map marker,
clear-line E interaction and a contextual touch action. It tops each carried
calibre's reserve up once, preserves magazines/chambers/reload progress and
surplus rounds, and restocks frag/smoke grenades, medical and field utilities.
Carried consumables are copied into the practice session, and use/restock cannot
spend purchased inventory or export free items to the profile. Stock is a reusable
EquipmentStock definition. Dry AI pilots can return for ammo. Touch pause and
callout controls are kept separate regardless of stylesheet loading order.

## Sector patrol assignments and physical coverage (2026-10-31)

Owner accepted formal sector patrols distinct from camp footprints. Local main
commit 9fa169a adds sector-patrols.ts and passes every district's named sectors
plus full curated/road anchors into the authority. Valid ground points are
sampled across each sector (up to 24 stops, at least 18 m spacing); sectors need
no camp. Worlds with named areas and no facility system can also assign patrols.
The allocator separates camp defense, sector patrol and attack squads, retaining
at least half the living regular population on offensive assignments when
neutral/enemy sites exist. Normal Marina 32-bot start: 20 attackers, four local
sentries, eight sector patrollers. Camp teams split two sentries/two patrollers;
additional squads cover other sectors. Explicit orders and existing vehicle/
airborne crews override support allocation. Legacy environments retain their
local camp patrol behavior. Camps outside named bounds use the nearest sector.

Per-faction coverage records actual same-level troop visits within 12 m of
sampled stops, including passing friendly infantry. Planned destinations,
blocked paths and soldiers on another floor do not count. Visits become stale
after 90 s; age/unvisited/fresh metrics appear in patrolStatus and the battlefield
benchmark. Friendly destination leases spread patrols; opposing leases are not
read. Arrival pauses, bounded travel leases and 60 s failed-stop backoff prevent
stranding. Dedicated squads can change sectors after their initial 180 s period.
Nearby sightings produce bounded ten-second investigations followed by fifteen
seconds of patrol, with pursuit confined to the sector plus a 12 m margin and
nearby contacts. At most two patrollers, and no more than half a side's patrols,
can respond within 110 m to a contested/damaged command camp before resuming
coverage. Small duty/sector snapshot fields are validated; coverage history stays
local to the authority. Spawn/reset releases claims and clears history.

Ground mission heights now use terrain and authored step-height support, not
vertical roof raycasts. Overhead roof colliders no longer exclude valid ground
spawn/capture slots. Initial broad occupancy filtering caused two legacy terrain/
pavement regressions; the final height-aware obstacle filter preserves those
spawn semantics. Tests cover reaching/capturing the console under a real canopy,
plus vehicle pavement exits and convex-earth shot shielding. Facility/project
docs describe the separation, sampled coverage limits and tuning behavior.

Final full suite passes 2,256 tests / 242 files. All 110 focused tests across 11
files and typecheck pass again in the isolated committed release. Eleven new
sector tests cover independent areas, troop budgets/casualties, unavailable
squads/orders, independent factions' claims, real/stale visits, failed legs,
bounded investigations, actual resumption under continuous sightings, reset and
snapshot safety, worlds without facilities and canopy capture. Real-scene 180 s
probes run Marina 32/64, Queenstown and Raffles with valid snapshots and patrols
beyond camp radius; Queenstown samples show response and subsequent resumption.
The browser sector smoke visits 71/142 sampled Marina waypoints in 180 s versus
58 on the same set in one previous-behavior headless run. This is one comparison
with differing navigation/combat timing, not a whole-map-area or statistical
coverage claim. The baseline captures only actual physical visits. Browser
screenshots include desktop/mobile coverage and destinations. Actual-engine
Marina gameplay passes at 32 and 64 bots, about 60 and 59 FPS respectively in
10 s samples, no runtime errors or paid/map requests. Touch entry follows the
prior Chrome pointer-lock limitation; this is not a mouse-lock regression check.

## Vehicle collision body jolts and camera shake (2026-11-01)

Local main commit `96cfd83` adds a directional, severity-scaled impact response
on top of the existing rebound/skid physics. The movement solver retains the
latest contact serial, approach speed and normalized impulse direction in an
optional impact receipt. Authority snapshots validate the receipt; rendered
snapshots release it at the contact tick, so shared passengers see one jolt
rather than repeated shake on every snapshot. Initial adoption, replacements,
teleports and travel arrivals establish a baseline without replaying old hits.

A small deterministic, bounded damped spring pitches/rolls/bobs the model;
a faster rattle rotates the mounted camera. First-person eyes follow their
rendered seat and receive a smaller extra rattle; third-person gets the camera
response separately. Physical position and stored look angles are unchanged.
Helicopter flight pitch is kept separate from impact pitch to avoid feedback.
The device reduced-motion preference suppresses both hull and camera motion.
Gentle wall pressure does not continually restart the effect, and reset clears
it. No sound changes or paid generation were needed.

## Subtle firearm camera vibration (2026-11-01)

Local main commit `8d838a1` adds a very small, deterministic 160 ms firing
vibration alongside the existing recoil. Each axis stays below 0.1 degrees,
including sustained bursts from all eight weapon families. Shots refresh the
pulse rather than add amplitude. Resolved recoil and stance/bipod support scale
it; ADS reduces it by 60%, with further inverse-magnification damping (offset
sights use 1x). Reduced-motion preference suppresses it. Successful player
handheld shots trigger it; dry fire, remote shots and mounted hull guns do not.
Switch, reset, travel/respawn and pause input cleanup clear the effect.

The effect temporarily rotates both world and foreground cameras only around
the draw passes, including scopes/reflections. A finally block restores exact
quaternions/matrices before gameplay resumes or HUD publication, even on a
render error. Existing recoil/compensation, actual aim, bullet direction, spread
and random sampling remain unchanged. No sound/audio generation changes.

source. New tests exercise sub-degree magnitude relative to existing recoil,
all-eight sustained cadences, non-stacking notifications, ADS/support/optic
attenuation, finite frame timing, settling/reset, zero reduced motion, exact
camera/ray restoration after normal and failing draws, and unchanged recoil

## Geometry-based gunshot echoes, inverse-distance impacts and dry pass-by snaps (2026-11-01)

Owner requested gunshot echoes that respond to nearby buildings, HDB corridors
and void decks, then asked to discuss impact attenuation before continuing.
Implementation/deployment was held during that discussion. Owner approved
inverse-distance amplitude (inverse-square intensity), with stronger nearby
impacts and a final cap. Local commits: `4530374` acoustic spaces/mix, `57687fd`
impact falloff, and `f248c7c` replacement pass-by assets/processing. No GitHub push.

Gunshot acoustics uses thirteen short probes against visible static rendered
geometry, with material hardness, nearby wall distance and several overhead
hits. Nearby façades create geometry-timed slapbacks; open covered decks have
a shorter diffuse response; close walls under a low ceiling create a denser,
longer indoor response. Real elevated Queenstown estate void-deck and gallery
points classify covered/enclosed. It is a bounded local approximation, not
full specular path tracing or an exact room simulation. The same source-space
profile is used for player, remote and vehicle reports; passenger/turret origins
are sampled at their firing position rather than a chase camera.

The ElevenLabs report's fixed outdoor tail is lowered after its initial attack,
then early reflections and a deterministic damped stereo convolution supply the
local response. Open sky has no added room response. Heavy-gun bass remains;
suppressors excite much less reflected sound. Impulses are cached per context
(max 16). Acoustic geometry is cached per emitter with motion/floor/TTL refresh,
a 96-emitter bound, and four remote probes per 100 ms; the local gun has priority.
Existing burst handoffs, mute/pause/stop cancel the convolution tail as well as
sources; a silent clock owns tail cleanup. A shared combat limiter now routes
gunfire, impacts and pass-bys together, fixing a reproducible full-auto .50 /
50 m impact overlap that previously exceeded digital full scale. Other cover
callers preserve their behavior; acoustics additionally ignores drill figures.

Impact gain is min(.82, 8 × material × resolved calibre/power weight × sqrt(energy)
/ max(1,distance) × fade). The smoothstep fade is 1 through 100 m and zero at
140 m. A standard concrete strike is .8/.4/.2/.1 at 10/20/40/80 m, with gain
halving (intensity quartering) per distance doubling outside the cap/far fade.
Material, power, travel delay, lowpass, panning and spent-round attenuation remain.

Owner then reported laser-like "pew-pew" cracks. Treated as the bullet pass-by
(the context of hypersonic cracks); an optional clarification was offered. Two
new ElevenLabs v3 pressure-snap takes and one separate soft air take replace the
old combined tonal takes. Snaps are trimmed to 35 ms, retaining their first
millisecond then decaying with a 4 ms time constant. The separate unpitched air
rush lasts at most 90 ms and plays at 10% crack gain; the much weaker filtered
slapback is 8% at 35 ms instead of the old 22% / 75 ms repeat. Original pitch
and playback speed are preserved. The longest actual layer owns cleanup.
Original cached takes and once-only receipts are retained; no ambiguous retry.
Three completed requests cost 5 credits each. Included usage before 1,315 /
40,000, immediate check lagged at 1,315, settled at 1,330: exactly 15 credits.

Final frozen `f248c7c` matches all 3,215 tracked files. Standalone typecheck and
64 focused tests / nine files pass, including intensity-vs-gain law, near-field
cap, far fade, real HDB spaces, cache/probe limits, impulse reuse, tail cleanup,
short snap manifests, separate air balance, source power and natural speed.
Actual Chrome/Metal checks pass four source-space types in the FPS engine;
36 single/burst rifle/heavy/suppressed renders across six spaces including actual
HDB points; 12 room/impact mixes; 40 flyby renders across four weapon profiles
and five lateral distances; guest normal/caught-up flight, dedup/cover/own-shot/
subsonic exclusions; and 256 impact renders with the inverse-distance law.
Maximum tested room/impact mix .8814, pass-by/gunfire mix .7437 and broader
impact/gunfire mix .8814. Zero browser runtime errors or paid playback requests.

Full frozen suite on `57687fd` before replacement pass-by assets: 2,558 passed,
one known Upper Thomson ground anchor failure (85,-14), no worker RPC errors,
using two workers and a 30 s test timeout. Final asset/voice code is covered by
the clean focused and browser runs; no full-suite pass is claimed. Initial QA
was interrupted by Vite re-optimizing dependencies; the final frozen QA uses
an untracked config with explicit pre-optimization and a separate cache. It
does not change the production Vite config. A first synthetic scene fixture
used a second Three instance; the final fixture uses the same canonical Three
as the engine and passes actual geometry classifications.

`09ba4a55-7166-4533-8ad6-4816fc1000d3`. Both blockplaysg.fun and workers.dev
match all 25 tested HTML/JS/CSS/service-worker/manifest/impact/pass-by/air files

## 2026-11-03 — Freedom Force Mythic stat audit

Read-only gameplay audit: resolved fitted cargo stats and evaluated hitDamage /
shotsToKillOpponent against drill, assault, tank and catalog armor targets through
each weapon's travel limit. Final damage is 64 / 82 / 105 / 72 / 160 for Soft
Power / Hard Power / Smart Power / Peace Offering / M200; base platform damage
alone omits the cargo build bonuses. Judgment: Soft Power is borderline Mythic
versus Two Eyes Open (lighter and a close assault body-shot breakpoint, but worse
cadence, magazine, recoil/recovery and reach); remaining four have defensible
Mythic specialties. Smart Power one-body-shots 100 HP through ~114 m and
one-head-shots tank-role armor through ~139 m. M200 retains one-body-shot kills
against assault and 100 HP ceramic targets through its 500 m limit, with heavy
round overmatch, but needs two body hits against tank-role armor.

Caveats: ideal hit breakpoints exclude aim time, bullet travel and misses. All
five FF families inherit the generic rifle spread/bloom defaults; scopes do not
provide a distinct precision cone. Standard analyseBreakpoints excludes enemy
issue, including these cargo rewards; existing cargo tests assert tier labels
and OICW superiority to XM8, not a complete cross-Mythic balance contract.

freedom-crates, armory-balance, armor-inserts). No gameplay edits, commits, push

## 2026-11-04: permanent default respawn and soft beam hover
Local main commit 026f418 supersedes the earlier structure-only respawn rule.
The real aerial respawn map now always lists this side's Default spawn alongside
allied structures. Manual selection remains available with no allied sites;
automatic respawn prefers operational allied structures, then falls back to the
default. The authority preserves the countdown, rechecks safety and cancels
blocked choices. It searches only the bounded default zone (centre + rings to

waits until clear rather than selecting an arbitrary remote point.

available portions select on the first pointer press. Grey beams remain rejected
by the authority. Pointer exit restores the resting state and keyboard focus

## 2026-11-04: dramatic vehicle destruction and drone ground explosions
Destroyed car and helicopter hulls now keep their
momentum: `damageVehicle` no longer zeroes velocity (boats still stop) and adds an
upward kick and spin; `stepVehicleWreck` in vehicle-rules.ts coasts, falls, bounces
once and skids out under friction, for both the local range and arena authority.
Snapshot validation allows yawSpeed up to 3 only on a dead hull. Land and air troop
transports coast too (internal driftX/driftZ, not replicated).

Presentation is new vehicle-wreck-motion.ts, read from replicated hull state:
cook-off blasts, a crash blast on contacts of 7 m/s or more (via the impact serial),
tumble, rotor spin-down and loss, and burn puffs. The engine drains
takeHullBlasts/takeHullBurns into combatVisuals.hullBlast/hullBurn. The old low-poly
explode was removed, and wrecks no longer use that particle pool.

Downed drones pop when hit and explode on ground contact, with a crater. Crash and
drone-ground explosions are visual only by choice; the one damaging hull blast
stays at the point of destruction, and "falls harmlessly" still holds.

Validation: typecheck passes. Full vitest 3060/3065; RespawnLoadoutSelector and the
cosmetic-wrap test also fail on clean HEAD, and arena-network, bot-difficulty-runtime
and regions queenstown pass when rerun alone under lower load. Review fixture:
scripts/fixtures/wreck-crash.html. An ad hoc real-engine run in isolated Chrome
destroyed a falling helicopter and a mounted car at 15 m/s (coasted 26 m, phase
defeated, no exceptions); it boarded via an injected interact call because the E key
did not mount in that headless run. Not run: LAN play in a browser (adoptShared is
unit-tested only), test:vehicles, and the transport crash visuals in a browser.

## Grenade throw and armor plate animations (2026-11-04)

Reworked both viewmodel animations. Throw (CS/CoD): `fps-grenade-motion.ts` is pure
and driven by the fuse clock: raise, left hand takes the pin, arm cocks while the

## 2026-11-04: scene of death before respawn
Falling now plays a death window instead of cutting straight to the respawn map
or a bare countdown. src/game/death-recap.ts holds the stats tracker and the
camera path (both pure and unit-tested); src/components/DeathRecap.tsx is the
panel; fps-engine's placeDeathCamera drives the shot.

Camera: the first-person view falls and rolls, then lifts to a vantage behind
the body with the killer beyond it. The side is fixed at the moment of death;
only the look follows the killer, who also wears a live name/HP tag. The lift
raycasts against scenery. Reduced motion holds the vantage from the first frame.
The player now has a real corpse (arena-runtime ownCorpse): hidden until the view
leaves the body, and never created when loading in already dead.

Stats, all from what the arena publishes so guests match hosts: killer, rank,
faction, weapon, range, HP they had left, damage you dealt them, top three damage
sources; this life's time, kills, damage, accuracy, distance, longest kill and
pay; session K/D; and notes such as nemesis, close call and personal bests.
hurtFrom gained by/cause (players only, to keep snapshots small) and ArenaFeed
gained cause; both are validated for guests.

Timing: expeditions hold the window for DEATH_WINDOW_SECONDS (4), skippable with
Space, Enter or the button, then show the respawn map. Arena matches hold it until
the respawn. The played game now keeps players down 6 s, not 3
(ARENA_PLAYER_RESPAWN_SECONDS, set by arena-runtime through
setPlayerRespawnSeconds). Bots stay at 3 s and createArena's own default stays 3 s,
which is what most simulation tests assume. Skipping never shortens the timer.

Validation: full vitest 3069 pass, 2 fail (RespawnLoadoutSelector 'Unlock the extra
main slot' and vehicle-rules wrap credits). Both also fail on a clean checkout
without this work. Under load many world tests exceed the 5 s timeout; the run above
used --testTimeout=120000. scripts/death-recap-smoke.mjs passes on swiftshader
(arena kill by a real bot, expedition hand-over, Space skip, auto-respawn, 390x844
and 844x390 fit), with screenshots in .cache/death-recap/. It slows the page clock
because a software renderer screenshots slower than the window lasts. Not exercised:
a two-browser LAN guest (only the validators are covered), or the 'defeated' screen
of non-arena exercises, which was left as it is. Not pushed or deployed.

## 2026-11-04: Marina quay rail and deliberate water entry
The quay rail had no collision and walking off any dry edge counted as entering the
water, so players walked straight through it. Fixed in src/game/swimming.ts, which is
player movement only: bots, vehicles, line of sight and the navigation bake never see
the rail, so the bake needs no rebuild.

Rails: MARINA_QUAY_RAILS (marina-water.ts) follow the rendered rail on all four sides,
are taller than a jump, and open only at the two jetties. The north quay had no rail
at all, so marina-scene.ts now builds one. A body stops at 0.38 m from the rail, which
is 0.76 m from the water and outside the host's 0.5 m touchesWater slow zone.

Decks: walking stops a body's width short of any deck edge. The ways in are a jump, or
walking through a ladder gate. Reaching the last body's width of a deck takes a jump or
a climb out, so a body there may step off. It could not jump from there because
grounded() is false, so blocking it would have stranded the player. marina-camp.ts adds
a kerb and rope along those edges, with a gate at each ladder. The rope is visual only.

Authority: arena-rules passes swimmer.move a `leaping` flag taken from the input's eye
height (above standing, or the swim pose), since that branch flattens y to 0. A hacked
guest can use it to leave a deck but not to pass a rail.

Validation: full vitest, swimming.test.ts gained three cases. A throwaway CDP drive in
the real engine on Metal (scratchpad, not in scripts/) confirmed the edge stop, jump in,
ladder in, the rail stop at z=30.76 with four jumps against it, and the host actor
following a jump to within a millimetre. dragon-boats-smoke passes. Not exercised: a
two-browser LAN guest, or touch input beyond the same engine calls. Nothing in game says
why the edge stops you, so a hint is a possible follow-up. Bots and cars can still clip
the rail visually, since it does not block them.


## 2026-11-04: respawn descent, and shaders built before the click
Choosing a beam on an expedition's respawn map now flies from the map camera down
into the eye, as the first entry does. deployment-intro takes the camera's current
pitch so nothing jumps, which means the first entry also leaves from the map's tilt
(about -1.28 rad) rather than snapping straight down. The shield is held for the
descent plus SPAWN_SHIELD_SECONDS and restarted on landing, and shieldOf caps what a
snapshot reports at SPAWN_SHIELD_SECONDS: guests' validArenaSnapshot rejects anything
higher, and would otherwise drop the host's whole snapshot for the whole descent.
Arena matches have no aerial map and get no descent. The AI pilot skips it.

The "freeze" was three things. Measured in headless Chrome on the real GPU with the
shader disk cache off, dev build (see the profile-hitches note in the session memory;
software renderers disable shadows and occlusion, which hides all of this):
- Picking a respawn beam dropped the game to `paused` with the mouse released, which
  looks like a freeze. The pause rules now exempt respawnDescent.
- Disposing weapon dress let three delete programs that the next dress wanted back,
  on the landing frame. keepShadersLinked holds them.
- Entering a district linked GTAO passes and figure shaders on the first frames.
  warmShaders now draws a real frame with occlusion and a stand-in for each faction
  and a player (arena-runtime standInFigures), then removes them in the same task.

The non-obvious part: night-exposure and world-night-lights each patch materials on
their own rescan timer (.5 s and 1.5 s), and every partial state and order of those
patches is a separate program. A figure could be drawn half-patched and link again
later. A wait on the map hid this; only a slow clock on a software renderer showed it.
Figures now take both patches on arrival via onFiguresAdded, in one fixed order.

Results, entering a district: links after the click 9 -> 0, worst frame 505 ms -> 41 ms,
long tasks none, 186 programs linked before the map, ready in about 3.6 s. Respawn pick:
0 links, worst frame 26 ms (measured before the warm-up and patching changes; the
smoke's link check on swiftshader still passes). Watched 25 s of play after landing
with 0 links on an earlier build of this warm-up; not re-run for that length on the
final patching. The earlier build's 68-76 ms frame just after the click was mostly
native browser work, and did not reappear in the final fast-click run.

Not covered: other late arrivals (vehicles and so on) still go through the timed
rescans and can link when first seen. Not measured on a production build or a
physical GPU; this machine is a VM with a paravirtual GPU. The OPERATOR / REDEPLOYMENT
caption is not exercised by a smoke, since death-recap.html uses the engine without
ExpeditionGame.

Validation: tsc clean. Full vitest 3074 pass, 2 fail (the same RespawnLoadoutSelector
and vehicle-rules failures as a clean checkout). death-recap, player-respawn and
deployment-intro smokes pass on swiftshader; the last needs DEPLOYMENT_SMOKE_PACE=12
there, or its short windows pass during a screenshot, and now fails on any shader link
between the click and landing. Not pushed or deployed.

## 2026-11-04: test suite fixes and manual deploy of 94a251d
The deploy workflow had failed at `pnpm test` on every run since b9ab5a7 (2026-10-31);
the site has been reaching production through manual deploys. Two tests were stale after
17570b9 made paid equipment rentals (RespawnLoadoutSelector text, vehicle wrap credits);
the game was right and only the tests changed. The rest were slow world tests timing out
at vitest's 5 s default, and which ones varied by run, so `pnpm test` now passes
--testTimeout=60000. Bare `pnpm vitest` still uses 5 s.

## 2026-11-05: spawn rack reworked to draw, hold and release
The spawn rack read as methodical: the handle sat at the rear stop for 0.34 s and the release sound played 0.24 s after the bolt was home.
A first pass (fast pull, hard slam, whole gun thrown forward) was rejected by the owner, rightly: hands are children of the gun, so the throw carried the hand 21 cm forward after it let go, and it looked like the hand was pushing the handle back in. Measure hands in view space, with the rig's movement, when judging this.
Now, on its own clock in seconds (READY_BEATS in fps-weapon-motion.ts): raised in 0.32 s, a 0.2 s draw, an 0.08 s still hold, then let go. The hand jerks back (cockingHandRelease: fastest at the first instant) as the palm opens with fingers fanned, and hangs until 0.98 s while the handle runs home alone in 50 ms. readyMotion holds the gun's pose until then and goes straight to rest, skipping the reload's forward kick. readyEnergy and readyViewKick add only a small tug and bolt jolt. Sounds fire on the same beats. The rack is 1.4 s, was 1.65 s, so control comes 3.55 s after the first descent frame, not 3.8 s; the spawn shield follows.
On request, the SAR 21's rack pose no longer turns its left side to the camera: the gun stays nearly square, and the butt dips about 7 degrees with the muzzle lifting on the draw, since the force goes into the back of the gun. These are topKeys, so its empty reload's charging step gets them too.
Only the SAR 21's top handle gets the full 13 cm jerk, a palm aimed at the camera and a forearm run out of frame (the stub ends in mid-air otherwise). Side handles keep their old 4.5 cm path, because on those a long forearm points at the camera and blocks the view; they get the hang and fanned fingers, and would need their own wrist poses for more. Hand changes are shared with empty reloads, which keep their long hold and forward kick. Review page: scripts/fixtures/ready-rack.html.
Validation: tsc, vitest, deployment-intro smoke on Metal headless Chrome, and a test on every non-belt, non-drum gun that the hand holds still, jerks back and does not come forward until it returns. SAR 21 frames checked by eye and in view-space numbers; P30, XM8 and M200 on contact sheets; SAR 21 empty reload on one frame. Not heard, as the VM has no audio, and how it feels has not been judged by the owner.

## 2026-11-06: flinch on being shot, for the player and for bots
On request. The player (`fps-flinch.ts`): a hit snaps the view up and away from the side it came from, peaking at 45 ms and gone by .4 s, render-only like the firing rattle and added to its pose, and moves the real aim, which is not handed back like recoil's. Strength follows health plus armor lost, full at half a bar or for any blast; a 17-damage rifle hit measured .3 to .4 degrees of aim and a .7 degree view peak in the real engine. Under 3 damage, piercing damage (gas, bailouts), vehicles and anything off `playing` do not flinch. The view part is divided by the square root of magnification and off under reduced motion; the aim part stays. Both damage paths flinch: the local `hurtPlayer` (range counter-fire, local blasts, vehicle blasts, now given a source) and the arena snapshot's `hurtFrom` for expeditions, arenas and LAN guests.
Bots (`BOT_FLINCH` in arena-bot-combat.ts): a non-piercing hit that leaves a bot alive multiplies its spread by up to 3.4, easing out over .45 s, and floors its next shot's wait at .12 s by strength, which never stacks, so a bot under automatic fire still shoots back. A second hit refreshes rather than adds. The rig's body flinch was already there. No randomness was added to the host, so seeded sequences are unchanged except where a wider cone moves a round.
Validation: tsc, full vitest (3,381), and a scratch CDP check (not added to `scripts/`) on Metal headless Chrome: a seeking pilot in a Queenstown expedition with health x40, 4 hits read from 16 ms samples of `canvas.dataset.flinch` and `hud.pitch`.

## 2026-11-06: aim assist you can feel on a phone

The owner could not feel the October assist on a phone: it only reshaped a
drag, so a resting thumb got nothing. Added **tracking** (`assistTrack` in
`aim-assist.ts`, `trackAimAssist` in the engine loop): while a touch session
has a thumb on the look surface or the fire button, the sights follow 60% of
the locked target's world bearing change per frame (strafing target or
strafing player), fading over the cone. It follows the eye-to-target bearing,
not the aim, so recoil is never paid off and `compensateRecoil` is not told.
Bearing jumps over 0.03 rad/frame (respawn, new aim point) are ignored.
Also stronger: slowdown 0.3→0.45, pull 0.2→0.3, cone 3 radii clamped
1.7°–6°. `hud.aimAssistLocked` tints the hip crosshair orange while locked,
so a phone shows whether the assist is engaged at all.
Validation: vitest, typecheck; headless Chrome with CDP touch on the Marina
range: locked a target, strafing with a thumb resting turned 0.066 rad to
follow, without a thumb 0. Not yet tried on a real phone.

## 2026-11-06: more graphics settings, for toning a phone down
On request. Settings › Graphics now has four presets (High, the default; Balanced; Low; Battery saver) and per-item controls, all saved per browser so a phone keeps its own mix. New store `graphics-settings.ts` (`blockplay-sg-graphics-v1`); sun shadows on/off, ambient occlusion and reduced effects stay in the environment store, and the presets set both. A preset is shown pressed only while every value matches; otherwise "Custom mix".
- **Resolution** 100/85/70/50% of each view's usual pixel ratio (`renderPixelRatio`; FPS cap is still 1.35, `FPS_PIXEL_RATIO_CAP`). Live in the FPS engine (subscription, then `resize()`); the passes already size from the drawing buffer. Region, Marina, World and MarinaWorld views take it at creation.
- **Frame rate limit** off/60/30 (`createFrameLimiter`, 1.5 ms early tolerance). A skipped rAF tick runs nothing, so the next frame takes the whole step.
- **Sun shadows** Off/Low/High: Low is a 1024² map instead of 2048² (`fps-sun-shadows` `update(..., size)` drops and reallocates the map; texel snapping follows).
- **Lens effects** (flare, haze dust, lens raindrops) skip `lens.present`; `data-lens` reads `off`.
- **Scenery reflected in sight glass** off skips `opticReflections.render` and zeroes `reflectionReady`.
- **Antialiasing** is read when a canvas is made, so it applies the next time a game starts (the FPS surface survives district changes).
Validation: tsc, full vitest, new `graphics-settings.test.ts` (sanitising, presets, limiter cadence at 60/120 Hz, storage). Settings page at 375 px in the browser pane: presets set both stores.
