## 2026-11-06: bots no longer stare at their boots and spin; finite turning
Owner report: bots sometimes looked at the ground and spun. Cause, in `stepBot` (arena-rules.ts): yaw and pitch were set every tick, instantly, to the bearing of `target` — which with nobody in view is the bot's own walk goal (patrol point, mission, last known contact). Full-stride steps with no arrival overshot that point (plus a 0.35 strafe made them orbit it), so the bearing flipped up to 180° a tick, and the `-.65` chest offset over a near-zero distance pitched them to about −90°. Measured over 60 s with 6 mixed bots at 20 Hz: one bot 25% of ticks pitched below −40°, 282 yaw jumps over 86° in a tick, 675°/s mean turn.
Now: `BOT_TURN` / `botTurn` / `botAligned` in arena-bot-combat.ts cap turning (9 rad/s yaw ≈ 515°/s, 5 rad/s pitch); a bot faces a contact, or a last known position more than 1.5 m off, else its direction of travel with level pitch, holding yaw when standing. It fires and builds `aimFocus` exposure only within 0.2 rad of the shot, so a long swing costs time. Unseen walk goals stop the bot within 1.5 m (`BOT_TURN.arrive`); a quiet patrol lingers 1.2 s there then picks its next point (standing still would quietly buff idle bots — the old orbiting carried the own-motion spread penalty). A patrol re-pick no longer flips `strafe` mid-dodge (latent: it reversed evasions). Client (arena-runtime.ts) eases avatar pitch as it does yaw. Same probe after: 0% downcast, no jumps, ~25°/s mean, bots still walk 93–175 m a minute.
Tests: new `bot turning` block (cap, short way round, alignment, arena regression). Two seeded tests were fragile, not wrong behaviour: the friendly-squad test needed a friendly alive at 160 s (at HEAD the squad dies by then for 2 of 8 step sizes) — it now makes its friendly-fire shot with the first friendly on the ground; the bot-damage test didn't allow a lethal hit to take only the remaining health. tsc, full vitest (3,407). Not checked in a browser arena.

## 2026-11-06: FPS counter / profiler overlay in Settings › Video
On request. Settings › Video › **Performance overlay**: Off (default), FPS counter, or Profiler (`perf-overlay.ts`, `blockplay-sg-perf-overlay-v1`, per browser, live). The profiler adds 1% low (99th-percentile frame), frame time and worst, main-thread time inside the frame callback, draw calls and triangles summed over every render call in the frame (it turns `renderer.info.autoReset` off while on and gives it back when off), geometries/textures/shader programs, drawing-buffer size and pixel ratio, Chromium JS heap, and a frame-time graph with 60/30 fps lines. The FPS engine, RegionGame, MarinaGame, MarinaWorld and World loops call `beginProfiledFrame`/`endProfiledFrame`; a frame skipped by the frame cap is not counted, and a gap over a second restarts the run. `PerfOverlay` is mounted in App, portalled into the fullscreen element when there is one, fixed below the HUD's top-left badge, and hides when no loop has drawn for 1.5 s (so never on menus). No GPU timer query: "main thread" well under the frame time means GPU-bound.
Validation: tsc, vitest (new `perf-overlay.test.ts`); full run had one failure, `building-lift-glass` cached ray queries, from the uncommitted ray-index work in the shared checkout. Metal headless Chrome, Marina range card: profiler 60 fps / 5.1 ms main thread / 1432 draws / 818k tris / 1728×1080 @1.35; switched to FPS and Off through the in-game Settings overlay live; no page errors. The hidden desktop pane reads ~4 fps, which is its rAF throttling. Not run on touch, a phone, in native fullscreen, or in an arena.

## 2026-11-06: open-world CPU cost: round index, hidden-subtree matrices, cover validation
On request, after profiling the open world on a 4x CPU throttle with the Low preset at phone size (the owner's mid-range phone stays slow on Low, so the CPU, not the GPU). Pushed as `48f313a`, `a1173cc`, `77f4fd7`.
- **Rounds** (`gameplay-ray-index.ts`): each round in flight raycast the whole scene every frame. A per-frame index over everything a round can strike gives each one only what lies near its path; tests compare it against the old recursive raycast. `scene-ray-index` now has `refresh()` and `query()` and refits moved entries in one pass (`ray-bounds-tree.refitMany`).
- **Cover** (`scene-cover.ts`, `matrix-epoch.ts`): validates its index once per run of code, and again after any `updateMatrixWorld`/`updateWorldMatrix` (counted by a wrapper on three's prototype). This resolves the `building-lift-glass` "cached ray queries" failure noted in the entry above, which came from an intermediate state of this work.
- **Matrices** (`visible-matrices.ts`): the weapon scene was 2,687 objects, 97% hidden, updated three times a frame. Matrix updates now skip hidden subtrees: always in the weapon scene, and in the world scene's renderer pass and pre-round pass. Explicit forced world updates still reach everything.
Function shares from the profiles: matrix work 16% to 7%, cover checks 3.3% to 1%. Correction: the fps figures first quoted (28 to about 38, also in the `77f4fd7` message) came from runs with weather and time of day on auto, which move the load a lot (bots fight less in rain). Controlled, sunny midday, 4x, old 8857b32 against new 4a26721 in the same browser: Toa Payoh 17.5/18.0 to 22.0/22.2 fps; Marina Bay 12.6/13.1 to 16.4/19.7 fps. Showers instead: Toa Payoh 28.4 fps on new code. Marina Bay 20 to 22 fps; then `4a26721` caches each moored boat's landing per step (`boatLanding` in arena-rules; `tryBoardDragonBoat` computed it for every bot before the range check, 36 `vehicleExit` calls a step), about 10% to 0.6%, 22 to about 25 fps. Marina's largest costs are now rendering (about 41%) and the bot simulation (about 25%). Static-scenery freezing was considered and dropped: the Merlion, set-piece trains and capsules, and the sun move outside `world.animate`.
Validation: tsc, full vitest (3,427), expedition-travel, pouch-reload, grenade-explosions, intervention-pouches and utility-wheels smokes. `fps-smoke`, `magazine-ammo-smoke` and `weapon-switch-audio-smoke` fail identically with these changes stashed (pre-existing).
Not covered: real phone; production build; other districts' frame rates; any unaudited code reading `matrixWorld` off a hidden world object between forced updates.
Follow-up measurement, sunny midday, 4x: bot figures are about 52% of draw calls in a Toa Payoh fight (477 of ~918 a frame, 23 figures in view; scenery 285) and 27% in Marina Bay (406 of ~1,512; scenery 966). Taking only the figures out of the camera's layers, still simulated and animated, raised Toa Payoh 25-26 to 35-38 fps and Marina Bay 18-22 to 27-28 fps, about 4-5 ms of world render per frame. That bounds what merging each figure into one skinned mesh could recover. Marina's scenery draw count is the other large lever.
Then `0a1b303`: arena and expedition figures are one skinned mesh (`createCharacterRig(..., { skinned: true })`; per-joint build kept for the first-person body and townsfolk). Figure draws 477 to 109 a frame in Toa Payoh, world render pass about 11.6-13 to 10.6 ms a frame at 4x: a few percent in fps, far less than the "figures not drawn" experiment suggested, because hiding figures by layers also removed raycasts against them and the impacts and blood that follow. Tests: per-vertex positions against the per-joint build in 13 poses x 21 looks, raycast hits/normals, culling bounds, no material shared between skinned and plain meshes. WebGL pixel comparison lit and thermal: at most 16 of ~30k figure pixels differ. Not covered: real phone, shadows on, scope reflection render.

## 2026-11-07: sun-shadow draws on the range: vehicle stand-ins, skinned range figures
Owner asked for these on every preset. Same probe and view as the entry above (Toa Payoh range, Balanced, 4x). Shadow pass 601 → 204 draws, main thread 13.0 → 10.9/10.8 ms.
- **Vehicles** (`shadow-proxy.ts`, called from `buildVehicleModel`): each rigid piece (the root, and each group named in `VEHICLE_MOVING_PARTS`: wheels, rotors, turret, steering wheel, gauge needles) gets one merged, shadow-only mesh; the ~120 parts per vehicle are marked `noShadowCast`. The stand-in keeps each part's shadow face and draws zero triangles except inside `onBeforeShadow`, so AO, thermal and the sight reflection never show it; raycasts ignore it (`Object3D` raycast, which `gameplay-ray-index` skips). Interior parts are included, so cab shadows are unchanged inside and out. WebGL comparison of humvee and helicopter with per-part casters vs stand-ins, outside and from the cab, sun at 15–70°: identical pixels (max channel difference 3/255). Anything that later moves or hides on its own must join `VEHICLE_MOVING_PARTS`. Dragon boats are untouched.
- **Range figures** (the two section soldiers and three visitors) use `createCharacterRig(..., { skinned: true })` like arena soldiers: about 92 shadow draws to 5.
- Tried and dropped: skipping casters smaller than one high-detail shadow texel (6.25 cm). It removed 27 draws (pistol serrations, sights, feed lips) with no measurable change in alternating A/B runs (10.8 vs 10.9 ms); a shadow draw costs about 5 µs at 4x here. The first-person body's 66 shadow draws (9 body, the rest pouches, magazines and the holstered pistol, whose visibility changes with reloads) are therefore worth about 0.3 ms; left as is.
Validation: tsc, vitest 3,465 (new `shadow-proxy.test.ts`), fps-pilot smoke. `vehicle-smoke` fails at "One wrap purchase fits both vehicles" (1535 vs 950 tokens) identically with these changes stashed.
Not covered: real phone; production build; arena/expedition vehicle scenes by eye (same model builder).

Arena simulation couples facility presence to damage, respawns, squads, logistics, vehicles and proxy delivery. Navigation bake-world duplicates expedition structure assembly; loader is district-keyed and geometry signature rejects mismatches.
Proposed staged plan: extract physical structure descriptors/prefabs from facilities; compose mode-specific structures/objectives/policies over district terrain; adapt existing expedition unchanged; route damage/interactions/bot goals/spawn/logistics through explicit mode services; add mode/layout identity to transport/state/navigation contracts; prove with a facility-free objective fixture before adding full modes. Shared physical structures must not mandate health/ownership/capture/production; objectives can exist without structures. Static layout first; runtime building/destruction that changes collision requires explicit navigation/ray invalidation later. Validate all-district expedition layout parity, movement/ray/damage parity, host validation and travel/reset/disposal, plus alternative mode with no facility side effects. Existing uncommitted range-damage work untouched. Audit only: no tests/typecheck, commit, push or deployment.

## Team Deathmatch — 2026-11-08

Implemented the requested first mode after the physical-structure extraction. Public Multiplayer now offers solo bot matches and host-selected 4v4 Team Deathmatch in Toa Payoh Dragon courtyard and Chinatown Smith Street. The host owns balanced human teams, bot fill to four, team scoring (30 points / 300 seconds), protected three-second respawns, friendly-fire rejection and rematches. Scores survive player departures. Blocked spawns wait and retry; initial spawns are side-specific, subsequent spawns consider occupancy, enemy proximity and rendered sightlines. Both teams use assault bots under the same kit/rank rules. Expedition and FFA retain their existing branches/defaults.

## 2026-11-08: faster traversal, running poses and useful grenade reach

Local main commit `f526689` fixes the FPS movement loop's loss of elapsed time
below 20 FPS. Infantry movement/slide/jump collisions now consume slow frames
in steps no larger than 1/60 s, with a 250 ms suspension cap. On-foot walk,
sprint, ADS, crouch and prone speeds are 30% higher; burden/food still apply.
Swimming and vehicles retain their existing speed tuning. Running body and
viewmodel use a shared footfall phase, a lower canted weapon carry and bounded
weight-sensitive swing; reduced motion suppresses oscillation. Held unpinned
grenades share a smaller running motion. Shared character rigs now have longer
running strides, higher knee lift and weapon swing with hands attached to their
grips. Bot AI still uses role-specific speeds plus situational escape/order
boosts; this change improves presentation, not its pace-selection policy.

Overarm grenade speeds now use 1.75x the original catalog values (frag 24.5 m/s,
up from 18.2); player throws get a 12-degree level-aim lift tapering to zero at
vertical aim. Underarm speeds and launcher ammunition are unchanged. A 30-degree
frag launch lands around 55.6 m; level player aim finishes around 35 m. White
smoke, red smoke and fogging wait for both fuse expiry and supporting ground;
wall hits do not trigger them. Fully cooked smoke also lands before activating.
Explosive cooking remains dangerous. Red smoke's mission starts at activation.

Validation: all 3,546 tests / 358 files passed, typecheck and production build
passed, plus a focused 95-test run. New real Chrome browser smoke
`scripts/fps-movement-reach-smoke.mjs` measured 25.394 m / 25.398 m for three-second
sprints at normal rendering / throttled 10 FPS. It verifies running weapon
motion, held smoke, landed smoke, sprint-to-fire and bot pose renders with no
browser errors. Screenshots were reviewed. Reproduce with Vite 5175 and Chrome
9244 (override FPS_APP_ORIGIN/FPS_CHROME_ORIGIN); set NO_PROXY for localhost.
Logs, measurements and screenshots are in `.cache/movement-reach-audit/`.

## Recoverable PWA update activation (2026-11-11)

Local main commit `426bf06` fixes the stale update-offer race: the old button
captured a worker and waited only for a future controllerchange, even if another
client had already activated it. The modal then stayed disabled indefinitely.
Acceptance now checks current controller/activation state, uses the latest waiting
worker, observes state/controller changes with a polling fallback, and rejects
stalled activation after 15 seconds. Store-owned applying/error state prevents
double submissions and restores Retry update on failure. No storage is cleared.
Seven regression tests cover already-activated/replaced workers, normal activation,
missed events, stalled retry, redundant workers and messaging errors. Extended
Chrome production PWA smoke passes normal acceptance, externally activated worker,
dropped activation message/retry, and offline behavior. Typecheck and all 3,835
tests / 398 files pass. Browser smoke needed NO_PROXY for localhost in this host.

all 3D/gameplay changes. No backend sync, account identity or automatic AI calls
are implied. Workflow and future server-storage direction: `docs/LEVEL-REVIEW.md`.

## Private Cloudflare review persistence (2026-11-11)

User authorized Cloudflare storage for the level review board. Local main
`c520614` adds private SQLite Durable Object persistence; `624c906` fixes
same-origin Vite-to-Wrangler forwarding for local development. No GitHub push.

`LEVEL_REVIEWS` / `LevelReviews` adds its own `level-reviews-v1` migration while
preserving PublicRooms. Bearer authentication is checked before storage access.
One project object (`design-v1`) stores the append-only review JSON, revision and
server update timestamp in SQL TEXT, transactionally. A separate verification
object isolates tests. GET/POST `/api/level-review` require the private credential;
streamed bodies are bounded to 2 MB, invalid/conflicting data is rejected, retries
are idempotent, and storage failures do not acknowledge a save.

Frontend uses the existing browser review as an offline outbox. Opening the
private link connects and merges local threads; the fragment credential is then
removed from the address bar. Sync preserves changes during request latency,
refreshes visible clients every 15 seconds and on focus/online, and shows pending,
acknowledged, offline and access/conflict states. Disconnect aborts requests and

## 2026-11-11 — draggable comment pointer and release-point confirmation

User found mobile pinning confusing and requested a draggable 3D cursor/pointer
with a Pin option at release. Local main commit `375d7fb`; no GitHub push.
Both map and model review now use ReviewPointer: drag or tap any point, release,
then choose the floating Pin here button. Initial center is not selected. No
composer or thread is created on drag/release. Real model raycasts save the
released mesh-local point and camera view; map transform saves world X/Z.
The 48px pointer follows the finger, stays visible after release, and can be
adjusted again. Background/out-of-bounds release, pointer cancellation, projection
resize and camera presets invalidate old choices. Pointer capture handles dragging
across edges; additional touch pointers do not replace the active gesture.

Models explicitly separate Position pin (camera fixed) from Move view (orbit).
Returning from view mode requires a new placement. Zoom/presets also reset it.
Keyboard arrows move the pointer, Shift increases step, Enter offers Pin here,
Tab reaches confirmation, Escape cancels. The canvas Enter shortcut focuses the
pointer instead of directly creating a center pin. Existing whole-model comments,
draft guards, surface/history schema and cloud persistence are unchanged.

## 2026-11-11 — Two-finger review controls shipped

User requested two-finger zoom/pan following draggable review pointers. Completed and manually deployed from main; no GitHub push.

- Local commit `fde95fa` adds touch pinch zoom and simultaneous centroid-following pan to map and model review, including active pin placement. New shared `use-review-gestures.ts` captures the second touch before orbit/placement, invalidates candidates, keeps remaining fingers locked until all lift, freezes/rebases extra fingers, and suppresses gesture compatibility clicks. Window pointer-up/cancel retires touches released outside the stage.

## 2026-11-12 — Marina Bay look trial (sky, haze, baked indirect light, grade)

Committed locally at the owner's request after reviewing the screenshots; no
push, no deploy. Dusk haze (too pink) and rain cloud gaps still need tuning. New
`src/game/district-look.ts` (+ test) holds an opt-in per-district look
(`scene.userData.districtLook`, or the scene kit's `look` option); only
`buildMarinaScene` opts in (`MARINA_LOOK`). Other districts are unchanged.

- Sky: gradient dome with sun glow, dusk horizon tint, dark night and blocky
  three-tone cloud cells that follow weather. Display colours, like the old
  clear-colour sky: in the post chain it is drawn on the canvas under the
  scene picture (`scene.userData.skyDome`, world-occlusion), so no bloom or ACES
  greying; on the plain path it is drawn first in the scene, untone-mapped.
- Haze: lit materials (the night-exposure patch) replace three's fog with
  height-aware exponential haze before tone mapping, towards the same sky turned
  into scene values by inverse ACES. Density follows the scene fog near/far.
- Indirect: daytime sky visibility (12 cosine rays, 70 m reach) baked into the
  blue channel of the existing night-exposure field after load, 4 ms per frame
  (~1 s total here), solid cells dilated from open neighbours, fades in over
  1.5 s. Scales ambient only; ground-coloured bounce in occluded places and on
  lower walls; wall-foot darkening reduced while GTAO runs.
- Grade: split tone, saturation and contrast in the output pass after ACES;
  the plain one-render path has none. `fps-engine` lens flare now compares
  against `atmosphere.lensSky(gradeApplied)` since the sky is no longer flat.
- Software renderers: no material splice and no daytime bake (three's fog towards
  the displayed horizon), clouds without edge filtering. Reduced effects (Low,
  Battery presets) turn clouds and baked indirect light off.

Evidence `.cache/marina-lighting/`: before-*/after-* (overview, street, dusk,
night, rain, canyon, towers, towers-dusk), indirect-on/off-*, sw-*, timing
reports, capture.mjs/probe.mjs/look.html. Real-GPU frame time +0.3–0.6 ms at
1600×900 (overview/street), rain/towers within noise. Not checked: phones,
MarinaGame walk/drive UI in a live session, LAN, thermal view by eye.

Tuned the same day after the owner saw dusk live: dusk air away from the sun is
now mauve (`DUSK_AIR`) with the warmth kept on the sun side, the dusk grade is
gentler, and overcast/rain clouds are a darker deck against the grey sky.
Evidence `.cache/marina-lighting/tune1-{dusk,towers-dusk,rain}.png`. Rain haze
still reads slightly cyan (the weather's own sky colour); left alone.

## Scope shadow driven by changes of motion (2026-11-12)

Uncommitted on main. `src/game/scope-shadow.ts` is now `createScopeShadow()`: a
two-axis underdamped spring (14 rad/s, damping .5, closed form so frame-rate
independent) kicked by changes in motion rather than held by strafe speed. A
steady strafe or turn keeps a 25% lean (about .045 lens UV); starts, stops and
reversals swing to roughly .12 to .17 and ring out with one small overshoot.
`createScopeRenderer` derives turn rate, pitch rate and vertical speed from the
world camera's own frame-to-frame movement, so flicks, recoil climb, jumps,
landings and stance changes all reach the shadow with no new engine plumbing;
the engine still passes only `lateralSpeed`. Raising the sight mid-strafe starts
settled, not kicked. Shader, clamp (.18), PiP camera and reticle are unchanged.

Focused tests (52, scope-shadow and weapon-optics) and typecheck pass.
`scripts/fps-scope-strafe-smoke.mjs` now samples the peak swing per frame and
passes on desktop and touch for Longwatch and Intervention in headless Chrome:
peaks .125 to .165, held lean .042 to .046, rebound on stopping, forward and
reduced motion clear. Pushed as `22e240c`.

### Eye box, tunnel, soft limit and true crescent (2026-11-13)

Uncommitted on main. The lens shader takes a new `scopeBox` uniform (radius,
softness) and draws the shadow as one disc that goes fully black; the old
lens-centred `clearCentre` mask now only masks the raise vignette. The central
44% of the radius is instead guaranteed on the CPU: `limitScopeEye` eases the
offset with tanh into `radius - soft - SCOPE_CLEAR_CENTRE`, replacing the hard
.18 clamp. `scopeEyeBox(magnification, relief)` hardens the edge (.15 to .08)
and raises sensitivity (.8 to 1.25) from 2x to 8x, following live zoom. A third
spring, `relief`, closes the box by up to .09 on a shot (`scopeRenderer.shot`,
called beside `firearmShake.shot`) or an abrupt vertical change (jump, landing;
gravity and looking around do not trigger it). Cache key is
`scope-reticle-v6-eyebox`. `canvas.dataset.scopeBox` added for smokes.

Focused tests and typecheck pass. `fps-scope-strafe-smoke` passes (peaks about
.12, lean .04 to .05). `fps-scope-glass-smoke` passes across nine scopes with
the centre still pixel-identical; its strafe check and the fixture were stale
after `22e240c` (they sampled a held strafe) and now sample the start swing.
The recoil and landing tunnel is covered by unit tests only, not seen in play.
Pushed as `576845f`.

### Turning: the gun trails, the shadow follows (2026-11-13)

Uncommitted on main. The owner found the turn shadow too fast ("zippy", a
little motion sick) and suggested the gun itself should turn more to justify
it; jumping was judged fine as is. The synthetic turn-rate and pitch-rate drive
is removed from `createScopeShadow`. Instead `createAimedTurnLag`
(scope-shadow.ts) gives a scoped gun a slow two-stage trail, up to .03 rad,
applied in `fps-engine.ts` as a rotation about the eyepiece lens so the reticle
stays on the aim point. Off for reflex sights, canted dots, vehicles and
reduced motion. `createScopeRenderer` adds a tilt term (`SCOPE_TUBE` = 4 lens
UVs per radian) because the eyepiece is so close to the eye that tilt alone
moved the shadow only about .015. Recoil tilt of the gun therefore shadows
more than before too. `canvas.dataset.aimedTurnLag` added.

Measured with real mousemove events in headless Chrome (Longwatch,
Intervention): a 0.6 s steady right turn builds the shadow smoothly to about
.078 and it eases out over roughly 0.8 s with no overshoot. Strafe and glass
smokes pass. No turn assertion was added to a smoke script.

## 2026-11-14 — Primary-source research: Crysis 3 dynamic water caustics

User explicitly demanded research after rejecting the cellular brightness effect.
Read Crytek's CRYENGINE 3 (not merely CE5) Water Volume Caustics documentation:
https://www.cryengine.com/docs/static/engines/cryengine-3/categories/1114113/pages/1048636
It documents surface-derived caustic capture including interaction ripples;
normal intensity/tiling during caustics-map generation; a grid-density control
(16–256), caustics map/G-buffer resolution (512/1024 defaults), distance and
stabilization snapping; and height above water for nearby objects/overhangs.
Do not confuse its Intensity parameter with post-hoc pattern brightness: the
manual specifically says it scales the normals used in generation.

Crytek's contemporary announcement explicitly lists Dynamic Water Volume
Caustics among Crysis 3's demonstrated features:
https://www.crytek.com/news/feast-your-eyes-on-a-new-cryengine-3-tech-trailer
CRYENGINE3 water shader doc confirms ambient FFT normals/heights plus propagated
interaction waves and warns against overdoing foam:
https://www.cryengine.com/docs/static/engines/cryengine-3/categories/1114113/pages/1048756
Deferred caustic processing is documented by Crytek:
https://www.cryengine.com/docs/static/engines/cryengine-3/categories/1114113/pages/1048590
These sources establish the structure/behavior, not the complete shipped Crysis3
shader algorithm. GDC2013 Sousa presentation located but no useful caustics
algorithm was established from it; do not claim otherwise.

Inspected Evan Wallace's original WebGL implementation as an independent,
implementable reference, NOT evidence of Crysis3's exact algorithm:
https://madebyevan.com/webgl-water/
https://github.com/evanw/webgl-water/blob/master/renderer.js
https://medium.com/@evanwallace/rendering-realtime-caustics-in-webgl-2a99a29a0b2c
Its caustics shader refracts rays through simulated surface normals, projects
the displaced grid, computes intensity from original/projected footprint areas,
and writes a caustics texture sampled by receiver shading. This provides a
concrete WebGL reference for deriving patterns rather than modulating a cellular
net. Above-water reflective caustics need a separate reflected-light treatment;
do not claim Wallace's underwater example already solves that.

Correct replacement direction: combine ambient and interaction surface normals;
generate a bounded light-concentration map from projected surface rays/grid;
apply to actual receiver lighting, including appropriate nearby above-water
walls/overhangs as well as underwater sand/steps. Preserve occlusion/distance/
shore constraints. Remove dependency on the arbitrary cellular pattern. First
acceptance scene should be plain floor+wall with decorative patterns and foam
disabled: a single actual shot creates propagating caustic bands. Then show
unamplified normal-FPS footage with splashes enabled. Pixel differences alone
are not acceptance. Current implementation cannot cast above-water caustics
because it runs only in water surface fragments over submerged receivers.

Video review limitation: CUA createBrowserTab/getState timed out (both kernel
resets); YouTube web fetch also failed. No footage was watched; do not claim
visual verification. Located example IDs j3BhfKbbCik and wGd82yuBEfI but they
remain unverified. CUA completion summary recorded. No code edits/deployment.

## One water shader for every district (2026-11-15)

Uncommitted in the shared checkout; nothing pushed or deployed. Before this only
Marina Bay and the Sentosa beach used `createWaterMaterial`; the other 17 districts
with water tagged flat opaque `MeshStandardMaterial` boxes with `markWater` and
animated pale "ripple" strips over them. Now every water mesh in every region wears
the shared surface shader (waves, Fresnel sky, glint, shot rings, rain rings, the
atmosphere's day/night and weather lighting). Districts get it from scene-kit's new
`water(color, { choppiness?, falls? })`, which wraps `createDistrictWater` (opaque,
depth-writing, no vertex swell because slabs have only corner vertices) and drives
`setTime` from `finish().animate`. Raffles calls `createDistrictWater` directly.
The decorative ripple strips and their animation are removed from 12 scenes.

Shader changes that also reach Marina/Sentosa: `USE_INSTANCING` in the vertex
stage (district water is batched), sun shadow reception through three's shadow
chunks (`lights: true`; body and glint dim under bridges, trees and boardwalks —
the old flat water took shadows, so this was a regression otherwise; the bay,
pond and beach meshes now set `receiveShadow`), and side-on faces: a slab's rim
is still, while `falls: true` (Changi's oculus column, Sentosa's water stair)
runs white streaks down the face. `district-boundaries` shares the district's
surface material for the sea past the boundary instead of cloning it; a clone
dropped `setTime`/`setLighting` and froze that sea at noon. night-exposure still
patches the literal `vec3 colour = mix(body, sky, fresnel);` line — keep it.

Ultra's bounded passes were extended to the other districts in the next entry.

Checked: typecheck; full vitest 432 files / 4322 tests; new `water.test.ts` cases
build every region and fail on any water mesh without the surface or off the
scene clock. New fixture `scripts/fixtures/district-water.html` (`show(id, eye,
target, {timeOfDay, weather})`, `waterReport()`), viewed in the desktop app's
browser pane (hardware GL): lakes, river, canal, sea, pond, rooftop pool, water
stair, waterfall, monsoon rain, night, a shot ripple, and the Ultra fixture
(`ultra-water.html`, plain and `?shallow`: refraction 1, reflections true,
glError 0). Not run: `pnpm build`, the CDP browser smokes (ultra-water,
shallow-water, dynamic/surface caustics, fps-district), and no in-game FPS
session or frame-time measurement.

Found, not fixed (present at d9008cc too): Jurong Lake's causeway deck is drawn
under the lake. ground-cover flattens the paving slab to ground level while

## Ultra water passes for every district with water (2026-11-15)

Uncommitted, same checkout; nothing pushed or deployed. Owner asked for the Ultra
passes beyond Marina and Sentosa.

What each kind of water gets:
- Planar reflection (the Water reflections setting, High or Ultra): every
  district. One capture at the primary surface's height, now bound to every water
  material in the scene and gated per fragment by `uReflectionBand` (0.02 for
  translucent bay water as before, 0.25 for opaque slabs, so a strait and the
  boardwalk water a step below it share the mirror; a rooftop pool does not).
- Ultra wave detail (`uUltra`): set on every water material, not only the primary.
- Interactive wave simulation (Ultra): every district's primary surface. Slab
  water is not a rectangle, so `water-waves` builds a 512² coverage map
  (`createWaterCoverageMap` in water-shore.ts) from the material's upward faces:
  distance from the bank stored as "depth", outline eroded one texel. It reuses
  the shore-depth uniforms, so waves settle toward banks, and `uWaterMask` makes
  the base surface and the 32 m patch ask the same covered-or-not question, which
  keeps the patch off islands, banks and bridge gaps with no holes. The base
  surface now also stays put outside `uWaveBounds` (the shared boundary sea).
- Refraction and caustics: still only Marina Bay and the Sentosa beach. They need
  something under the surface; district water is an opaque slab 12 cm over the
  lawn base plate, so the snapshot would show a flooded lawn. `water-surface-pass`
  takes its snapshot only for a translucent primary and exposes `visible` for the
  wave pass. Extending these means authoring beds per district.

Primary surface: `primaryWaterSurface` still honours `scene.userData.primaryWater`
and the Marina default name; otherwise it picks the largest water mesh (over
400 m²) by `waterSurfaceLevel`, which reads the dominant height, bounds and
outline from upward faces because ground-surface ownership re-cuts slabs into
one "owned surfaces" mesh whose origin is not its surface.

Cost, Jurong Lake at 1000×640 on this VM's paravirtual GPU, High → Ultra with
reflections: draw calls 278 → 373, triangles 201k → 439k, textures 7 → 10
(reflection target, two 512² half-float wave targets, one 512² byte map). Frame
time was too noisy here to state beyond "about a millisecond more"; treat as
relative. High with reflections off is unchanged in draw calls.

Checked in the browser pane via `scripts/fixtures/district-water.html`
(`show(id, eye, target, {detail:'ultra', frames, ripple:[x,z,strength]})` now
renders through `createWorldOcclusion`): Jurong, Woodlands (bridge gap stays
dry), Bishan (road crossing dry), Geylang canal, shot impulses in the patch;
`ultra-water.html` plain, `?marina`, `?sentosa`, `?shallow` unchanged
(refraction 1, reflections true, glError 0; `?shallow` diff 126741 as before).
Not run: the CDP smokes (ultra-water, shallow-water, caustics, fps-district) and
no in-game session.

## 2026-11-15 — Surface detail on the carried guns

First-person guns now get tiling surface textures on top of their flat
materials. New module `src/game/weapon-surface.ts`; tests in
`weapon-surface.test.ts`.

- Three families, sorted by material name with a metalness/roughness fallback
  (`surfaceFamily`): steel, polymer, rubber. Glass, lenses, sight dots,
  cartridges, physical materials and anything transparent are left alone.
- Per family, two generated `DataTexture`s shared by every gun: a packed map
  (R cavity occlusion, G roughness where 128 means unchanged, B metalness) and a
  detail normal map. Steel is 512 px over 16 cm, polymer 256 px over 6 cm,
  rubber stippling 256 px over 2.6 cm (`SURFACE`).
- The guns have no usable UVs, so the shader hook projects along the three model
  axes (six texture reads a pixel). It multiplies the material's own roughness
  and metalness and bends its normal, so skins, accents and wet weather still
  apply. It chains any earlier `onBeforeCompile` and adds `|weapon-surface-v1`
  to the program key; textures and tuning are uniforms, so families share a
  program.
- Applied only through `dressCarriedWeapon` in `armory-visuals.ts`, which
  `fps-engine.ts` now calls in place of `dressWeapon`. The armory preview, range
  racks, thumbnails, enemy and third-person guns are unchanged.
- `scripts/fixtures/weapon-lineup.html?surface=1` shows it on any platform.

Things to know: the occlusion channel is micro-cavity shading that matches the
normal map, not baked ambient occlusion of seams and recesses; that still needs
a per-vertex bake. Grain under about a millimetre is below a pixel at carry
distance, so in play the visible change is the grip stippling, the polymer
pebble and uneven highlights on steel. There is no graphics setting gating it.

Checked: `pnpm test` (435 files, 4,385 tests), `pnpm typecheck`; the line-up
fixture, and the Marina Bay range through CDP on the 5175 server (SAR 21 and
P30, hip and inspect) with no shader or console errors. Not measured: frame
cost on a real GPU or a phone. Not run: the browser smokes.

Pistol grip (2026-11-15): `besideGrip` takes a `fit` (rise, reach, fingers, arm, thumb). On the P30 the
firing hand sits .019 higher, under the tang with its first finger in the guard; the support hand is .016 ahead and
wraps over the firing fingers instead of through them; both forearms drop away steeply. The wrist band is no wider
than the hand (`w * .5`) and the gun-hand wrist is slimmer. From the first-person hip view the hands are still mostly
behind the wrists: the forearms are thick for the hand and the pistol sits low and far out in the shared hip pose.

Forearms (2026-11-15): `forearmGeometry` is no longer a cone with two torus rings (it read as bamboo). It is an oval
tube, narrow at the wrist, widest about 0.2 m down, with shallow folds winding round the sleeve; the wrist band follows
the hand's flat section. Hand size is unchanged (about three-quarters of life size against the guns).

## 2026-11-15 — Ambient occlusion on the first-person gun

The carried gun and hands now get their own screen-space occlusion, so a part
standing on another (the SAR 21 scope on its flat top, a hand round a grip)
darkens where they meet. New module `src/game/viewmodel-occlusion.ts`; tests in
`viewmodel-occlusion.test.ts`.

- Why a separate pass: the world's GTAO runs on the world only, the view scene is
  drawn afterwards over the finished picture, and its lights cast no shadows.
- Each frame, `prepare()` draws the view scene's opaque parts depth-only at half
  the drawing buffer (`VIEW_OCCLUSION.scale`), then works occlusion out from that
  depth: normals from depth, 12 spiral samples, 6 cm radius.
- A full-screen plate lives in the view scene. It is transparent with the lowest
  render order, so three draws it after every opaque part and before glass,
  reticles and effects; it multiplies the canvas, and a `GreaterDepth` test at
  the far plane keeps it to pixels the gun or hands covered. Its shader does a
  4×4 depth-aware blur.
- `hideNonOccluders` hides transparent, non-depth-writing, line and sprite
  objects for the depth pass and they are shown again straight after.
- Gate, in `fps-engine.ts`: the gun is visible, not the overview, the same
  occlusion setting and time-of-day flag as the world's pass, no thermal and no
  NVG aiming. `canvas.dataset.viewOcclusion` reports it.
- Same pass: `weapon-surface.ts` now fades its normal and cavity strength to
  nothing within 6 cm of the eye (full at 32 cm). At aim the SAR 21's flat top
  read as coarse green noise; the relief is sized for carry distance.

Things to know: it costs a second, depth-only draw of the view scene each frame
plus two half-size full-screen passes. Occlusion is on only in presets that have
the world's occlusion on, so Balanced and below skip it. A headless Chrome with
default settings has occlusion off; set `occlusion: true` through
`setEnvironmentSettings` to see it.

Checked: the Marina Bay range through CDP on the 5175 server with occlusion on
(SAR 21 hip, aimed and inspected, P30), no shader or console errors. Not
measured: frame cost on a real GPU or a phone. Not run: the browser smokes.

Life-size hands (2026-11-15): the gun hands are scaled 1.25 (`HAND` in `fps-viewmodel.ts`) and the free hands 1.18
(`HAND_SCALE` in `fps-viewmodel-hand.ts`), both about 78 mm across the palm. Each is scaled about the palm's face, so
every authored pose and held object still meets the palm where it did; the gun hand's palm stays `children[0]` because
tests measure it. The CIS 50's spade grips close all four fingers right round (`tight` in `curlFingers`). Seen in the
fixture on all eighteen guns, both hands, reload frames on SAR 21, P30, XM8 and the bolt gun, and in
`utility-animation.html` (frag, finale shell, bandage, first-aid kit, ammo pouch). Not seen in live play.

Selector artwork preload (2026-11-16): the next-gen home menu (title screen included) now fetches and decodes the
seven mode illustrations and `operations.jpg` after the page's `load`, through `preloadModeArtwork` in
`src/lib/menu-artwork.ts`, which also now holds `MODE_ARTWORK`. The image elements are kept for the life of the page,
so the panels' CSS backgrounds reuse them without a request. Skipped for Classic and when the browser asks to save
data. Seen through Playwright on a 4 Mbit/s throttle: no image request after clicking Single Player or Multiplayer and
the artwork is in the first screenshot (140 ms); without the change the panels were blank at that point. Not run: the
browser smokes.

**Swimming animation (2026-11-16).** Swimming had no hands: the rig was hidden and the eye bobbed on a sine.
`fps-swim-hands.ts` adds a first-person breaststroke and a treading scull with the free hands, the stroke sound on
each pull (was a 1.25 s timer) and a head lift with it (`swimMotion`, off under reduced motion). Wired in
`fps-engine.ts` beside the mantle hands. Hands go under when the sidearm is shown. Seen in `hand-models.html?swim=`
and in the real engine through `dragon-boats.html?swim` (stroke, tread, sidearm); `pnpm test:swimming`-style CDP
smoke not run.

**Swimming: backward stroke, sidearm strokes, one-handed aim (2026-11-16).** Going backward the hands now push the
water away from the chest (`BACK` keys, `state.back`) and the head leans back. With the sidearm selected the rig stays
visible in the water, its support hand hidden, and the left swim hand strokes alone; the pistol rides muzzle-up going
forward and levelled going backward (rig offsets beside the weapon tuck in `fps-engine.ts`). Buff: a still swimmer can
aim the sidearm (one-handed), scatter `SWIMMING.aimSpread` .03 against .085 at the hip; `ArenaInput.aiming` carries it
to the authority (`swimAiming`), optional so older clients still validate. Touch shows the Aim button when
`swimCanFire`. `scripts/swimming-smoke.mjs` now expects the aim to be allowed but was not run. Seen in the real engine
through `dragon-boats.html?swim` on touch input; multiplayer not exercised beyond unit tests.

## 2026-11-17 — Level review: drawn routes, areas, sightlines and verdicts; Marina reading posted

Owner's brief: past level-design passes added geometry without analysing the
layout, and Marina still reads as landmarks strewn on a flat plane. New working
agreement: the AI first draws its reading of a district on the review board
(what exists, what is wrong, what it proposes), the owner answers each thread
with a verdict or a redrawn route, and **no proposal is built before the owner
agrees with it**. The owner has no access to this host, so everything goes
through the deployed board (`blockplaysg.fun/debug?review=<district>`).

- Schema (`src/game/level-review.ts`): `anchor.shape { kind: route | zone |
  sightline, tone: existing | problem | proposal, points [{x, z, y?}] }` and
  `verdict: agree | disagree | rework` on an event. Level threads only; the shape
  is part of the immutable header. Shared by client, Worker and CLI, so an older
  cached client conflicts until it updates, as with `space`.
- Board: tone chips above the map, drawings on the schematic (SVG) and in the 3D
  layout (`buildDistrictShapes` in `district-review.ts`, no depth test, thickness
  follows camera distance, tagged `fpsEffect` so picking ignores them), "Add a
  point" in the compose form to draw by hand, verdict buttons under the reply box.
  Usage in `docs/LEVEL-REVIEW.md` ("Routes, areas, sightlines and verdicts").
- Marina reading: 17 threads `marina-read-*`, `marina-prob-*`, `marina-plan-*`
  pushed to the cloud board with `level-review-cloud.mjs push`. Numbers behind
  them, from the built colliders on an 8 m grid at eye height (boxes only):
  buildings are ~6% of the land, raised floor 3.5%, mean visible share of ground
  within 120 m is 59%, the south third 70-90%. Proposals awaiting a verdict:
  three lanes between the command posts (Esplanade, Helix Bridge into the
  museum, promenade through the hotel concourse), ArtScience opened as a
  two-level hinge linked to the podium roof, the Supertree grove moved onto the
  south lane, the south field rebuilt as two streets and a square.

Checked: typecheck, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, `district-review-smoke` and
`level-review-smoke` on SwiftShader, and by hand: drawings and tone chips in both
views, a hand-drawn area, a verdict. Not run: `level-review-cloud-smoke`,
touch drawing on a phone, `test:browser`/`test:pwa`/`test:touch`. The analysis
script is not in the repo; it dumped `world.obstacles` from a throwaway vitest
file and ray-tested boxes. Worth making a real script before the next district.

## 2026-11-17 — Ground detail pass: slab joints, asphalt patches, road paint

Owner asked for more world detail within the blocky style, without decisions
on their side. First of two planned passes (ground now, buildings next).

- **Slab joints** in the district look's surface shader (`paving` in
  `SurfaceVariation`, `LOOK_SURFACE_*` in `district-look.ts`): 4 cm joints on a
  1 m grid plus a small per-slab tone, on grey up-facing ground. Asphalt-dark
  ground gets sparse repair patches. Off with the rest of the surface pass on
  low detail.
- How the shader knows what is paving: merged ground caps now carry a
  `lookGround` vec3 (world X, world Z, the cap's narrower side) from
  `ground-surface-ownership.ts`; other geometry reads zero and falls back to the
  scale of a unit box, for raised decks and roofs. Under 2.5 m across gets
  nothing, which is what keeps road paint, vehicles and furniture plain.
- **Road paint** in scene-kit's `streetGrid` (19 kit districts): gutter strips,
  solid edge lines, and at grid junctions zebra crossings and stop lines.
  Flat paint only; no colliders.
- Marina's promenade is already separate 1 m slabs, so it is unchanged. Marina,
  Raffles and Queenstown roads are hand-built and have no new paint.
- Cost: about 100 ms more build time per kit district and 4-12% more triangles
  (the asphalt cap is cut round each painted stripe); one more material.

Checked: `pnpm test` (443 files, 4,423 tests), typecheck, build; by eye on the
real GPU through `district-water.html` in Bishan, Chinatown, Tuas, Sentosa and
Marina at street level and from 40 m. Not measured: frame cost. Not run: the
browser smokes, night or rain views, a phone.

Next in this line: building pass (ground-floor bays and canopies, roof parapets
and rooftop clutter), then façade furniture and ground decals.

## Vegetation pass (2026-11-19, a separate session from the building work above)

Owner asked for non-controversial vegetation improvements: looks and reactions only, no
change to cover, colliders or sightlines. What already existed and was left alone: tree
wind with travelling gusts (`tree-wind.ts`), falling leaves (`ambient-drift.ts`), wood and
foliage impact debris, marks and sounds (`fps-surfaces.ts`, `impact-audio.ts`), and the
researched species props (`vegetation-props.ts`).

Plants react (first piece):
- `foliage-disturbance.ts`: per-scene uniforms for up to six "hits" and four "bodies".
  `disturbFoliage(scene, point, radius, strength)` is called by `fps-effects.ts` `impact`
  (every surface strike; 2.6 m on leaf or wood, 1.5 m otherwise) and by
  `combat-event-visuals.ts` `blast` (16-20 m). `world-atmosphere.ts` advances its clock
  and empties it under reduced effects or reduced motion.
- `tree-wind.ts` (key `tree-wind-v3`): tree parts are thrown from a hit and ring back in
  about two seconds, leaves shiver; depth, distance and thermal materials follow. Each
  tree also leans up to 3.5% of its height, fixed per tree, in the shader only.
- `ground-cover.ts` (keys `ground-grass-v2`, `ground-grass-far-v2`): grass used to sway
  in unison at a fixed strength, each tuft along its own axis. It now leans downwind by
  `grassWindLean(wind)` in fronts that travel like the trees' gusts, with metre-scale
  waves; a blast lays it flat away from the centre; the player on foot, the car and the
  helicopter part it (`setFoliageBodies` from `fps-engine.ts`).
- Nothing reads the deformation back: hit tests and movement use authored geometry.
- `scripts/fixtures/vegetation.html`: any district, weather and hour, with `veg.hit` and
  `veg.bodies`.

Plants vary (second piece, same session):
- `treeTint(x, z, part, leaf)` in `tree-wind.ts`, written to each batch's `instanceColor` by
  `batchTrees`: per-tree value and warm/cool shift, per-part +-5% on crowns, value only on
  trunks. No geometry or collider changes; kit crowns are not `visualCover`, so they stop
  bullets and their shapes were deliberately left alone (see ideas below).
- Grass (`ground-cover.ts`, keys `ground-grass-v3`, `ground-grass-far-v3`): blades in a tuft
  are 1 / .7 / .85 long and splayed; colour drifts in broad patches and per tuft; near tufts
  carry a two-triangle flower head (`grassBloom`, define `GRASS_BLOOM`) that the shader keeps
  on about one tuft in six inside drifts and colours white, yellow or pink. Near tufts are
  now 11 triangles, not 9; far tufts unchanged.

**Character heads and faction silhouettes (2026-11-19).** The owner's "sphere" was the face: the head was an
ellipsoid with dot eyes. `character-rig.ts` now builds a faceted skull (`HEAD_RINGS`) with brow, eyes with whites, nose,
cheekbones, lips, chin, ears and separate hair pieces, and faceted hats, from `character-shapes.ts` (`loft`, `taper`,
`faceted`). Joints, dimensions, IK and every animation are untouched; hit spheres are untouched. Faction cues that do
not depend on colour: armed forces get a brimmed helmet, a longer pale bedroll and pale gaiters; Black Kite a taller
ridged helmet and a pale box kite on a mast behind the left shoulder. Everything new sits inside the hit spheres
(tested). Cost per arena figure, skinned: 2-3 draws before and after; triangles down (armed-forces rifleman R2 5,366 to
4,556, Black Kite 5,616 to 4,348). No frame timing was taken. Fixtures: `character-lineup.html`,
`character-district.html`. Limits seen in Tampines captures are written up in docs/FACTIONS.md: at night past about
18 m the two main sides are both dark shapes. Not built: per-person face variation (nose, jaw, brow widths from the
id hash), facial hair, faceted limbs and torso to match the head, a blink, an emissive or reflective faction marker
for night. Owner's calls: whether the health bar keeps the role colour, and whether night needs a lit marker.

Range load freeze fixed (2026-11-19, owner reported the live-fire range stuck on "Preparing the range" with the whole browser frozen):
- Cause: every windowed material compiled all 32 shop designs. On SwiftShader the longest
  load stall at Marina Bay grew from 12.8 s (before the shop work, `18efd0e`) to 35.4 s
  (`ac0f94c`). On a real GPU that is the GPU process, hence the whole browser.
- Fix: `pruneShopBranches` empties every `if (shopKind == N ...) {` block a program cannot
  draw: a shop wall keeps its own list, generated windows keep the district's `shops`
  only when `boutiques` > 0. Marina Bay's stall is 17.5 s after it, Orchard's 2.7 s.
  Key `-windows-v21-<used shops>-<room use>`.

shop tests are not pruned). Measured on SwiftShader only; no Metal context was free.

- `pruneRoomBranches` cuts hotel, factory and school blocks a program has no share of, and

Menu shader warm-up (2026-11-19, owner asked for it at the start screen with a loading bar at the top):
- `shader-warm.ts` replays `/shader-warm.json` in a hidden 1x1 WebGL2 context, one program at a
  time, from the first idle moment of any menu or debug screen. `ShaderWarmBar.tsx` is the bar
  ("COMPILING SHADERS 37%", then "SHADERS READY"). `createFpsSurface` holds it while a game
  renderer exists. One pass per list id (`localStorage` `blockplay-shader-warm`).

  build): own static server on `dist`, own headless SwiftShader Chrome, hooks `linkProgram`,
  loads `/debug?tool=fps&district=` for marina-bay, bishan, chinatown. 251 distinct programs,
  1.28 MB raw, 89 KB gzipped. The deploy workflow runs it after the build with
  `continue-on-error`; the file is never committed. The service worker bypasses it.
- Measured on SwiftShader, built site, fresh profile each: Bishan range ready in 36.6 s cold,
  23.8 s after the menu pass (which itself took 12 s). The same gain as a second load in one

matches what three generates on a player's GPU and graphics preset, which decides the hit rate
there; the CI step itself, which first runs on this push. Not covered: arena, expedition, night
and weather programs. SwiftShader has no KHR_parallel_shader_compile, so there each link blocks
the page for 100-200 ms; browsers with the extension poll instead. Browser smokes that count
programs should set `window.__noShaderWarm = true` before the page's scripts.

### God rays made visible — 21 November 2026

Owner asked why god rays were hard to see. Cause: `sun-rays.ts` masked a 0.32-screen
soft blob and averaged it along the march (about +10/255 half a screen from the sun),
and faded rays on anything nearer than 35 m. Now: sky-only mask, a hot disc + dim halo
source evaluated in the scatter pass, each pixel normalised by the same march over open
sky (visible share squared × `exp(-1.9·distance)`), near fade 0.5–10 m at 45%, sun up to
~0.4 screens off-screen still throws shafts, elevation ramp 0–3° (was 0–6°). Still additive
after tone mapping, so the lens-flare sky test is unchanged. Three passes, same buffers.
Typecheck, 22 focused tests, `sun-rays-smoke` and `sun-rays-lens-smoke` pass on ANGLE Metal
(Vite 5175, own Chrome 9461, stopped). Gameplay smoke not rerun. Docs: `docs/SUN-RAYS.md`.
Suggested next, not started: a real sun disc, a moon disc/phase/stars, and Ultra-only
volumetric (shadow-map marched) shafts for off-screen and overhead sun.

## 2026-11-21 — PWA update blocked by an in-flight request

Owner saw "The update did not finish" with `TypeError: Failed to fetch` at
`sw.js:1:2082` (`cacheFirst`'s network fetch). Cause, reproduced in headless
Chrome against `dist`: the browser will not activate a `skipWaiting()` worker
while the active worker still has an open fetch event, and a media download
stalled mid-body or before headers keeps one open, so the 15 s activation wait
expired.

- `src/sw/service-worker.ts`: `cacheFirst` tracks an `AbortController` per
  network fetch until the body is delivered or stored; a `RELEASE_FETCHES`
  message aborts them. A failed fetch now answers `Response.error()` instead of
  rejecting, which also removes the console line.
- `src/lib/pwa.ts`: `activateServiceWorkerUpdate` posts `RELEASE_FETCHES` to
  `registration.active` 2 s after `SKIP_WAITING` (`FETCH_RELEASE_DELAY`) if the
  update has not activated.
- `pwa-smoke.mjs` has a step for it; `docs/PWA.md` updated.

The fix lives in the page and the outgoing worker, so the first upgrade *to*
this build still runs the old code and can stall the same way; Retry works once
the stalled request ends, or close and reopen the app.

### Moon rays — 21 November 2026

Owner asked for moon rays. `SunRayLight.moon` (0–1, `moonRayAmount`: sun −4° → −10°) lets
`projectSunRays` run after dark at half the sun's strength along the moon key direction;
twilight between has none. Same passes; NVG/thermal/reduced gates unchanged. No moon disc
exists, so open sky shows a soft glow at the moon. Typecheck, full suite (4,511), ray and
lens smokes pass on ANGLE Metal. Gameplay smoke not rerun.

### God-ray glow follows cover — 21 November 2026

Owner: the ray glow read as an oversized lens flare and hid the beams. `sun-rays.ts` now
measures cover in a 1×1 pass (`Sun ray cover`): clear sun → small tight glow (35%, exp(-6d));
4–30% of the source hidden → long beams (exp(-1.9d)), hollowed within ~0.08 of the sun;
`RAY_GAIN` .6. Lens flare code untouched. Typecheck, ray tests, ray and lens smokes pass on
ANGLE Metal; full suite run before push. Gameplay smoke not rerun.

### The gun blocks the god rays — 21 November 2026

Owner asked for the rays to interact with the gun. `sun-rays.ts` `render` takes a `SunRayBlocker`
(scene + camera); after the sky mask it draws that scene's opaque parts into the mask as a flat
black silhouette (`hideNonOccluders` from viewmodel-occlusion, so glass/reticles/flashes pass

scene. The gun counts as cover, so a clear sun crossed by it switches from tight glow to beams.

Carried gun takes sun shade (2026-11-22, owner: "check if shadow maps are applied to guns" → "yes, add it"):
- The view scene (gun, hands) never had the sun's shadow map; under a roof the gun stayed sunlit.
  `viewmodel-sun-shade.ts` traces the eye-to-sun line both ways about 15 times a second through `roundIndex`,
  counts only meshes the shadow pass draws (`castShadow`, or a vehicle part behind a shadow proxy), eases the
  answer (~0.09 s) and `lightView` multiplies `weaponLight` by it. Off, and fully lit, while sun shadows are off
  (setting or software renderer). `canvas.dataset.weaponSunlit` reports it.
- It is one answer for the whole gun, not a shadow map on it: a shadow's edge does not cross the gun, and the gun
  throws no shadow of its own.
- Checked: unit tests, full suite, typecheck; about 0.2–0.7 ms a sample in Tampines, Orchard and Bukit Timah
  (node, no instanced accelerators). On the VM's Metal GPU the Tampines and Orchard ranges read 0.00 at dawn
  (behind the blocks) and 1.00 at dusk, afternoon and morning, with the gun visibly darker at dawn.
  Not checked: walking across a shadow's edge in play (CDP key-holds barely moved the player), vehicles, a guest.

Rain is one fall, not near and far groups (2026-11-22, owner: the near-to-far transition was obvious, far drops fell slowly):

Rain's CPU cost (2026-11-23, owner: slowdowns in rain, worst in a helicopter; "do fixes 1-3"):
- Measured first (Orchard, Ultra, Metal, uncapped): storm 21 ms a frame in the cockpit against 4.8 ms in sun. It was
  the rain update, not the reflections (a half-resolution screen-space pass; off made no difference): every drop asked
  where it lands every frame, and over a vehicle that was a raycast against each exterior mesh.
- `vehicle-rain.ts` draws each rigid piece's top surface once into an 8 cm grid in its own frame (hull, and each of
  `VEHICLE_MOVING_PARTS`, now in `vehicle-moving-parts.ts`), so a query is a transform and a read wherever the vehicle
  is. Cells are solid columns: leaning, rain meets a roof's edge where a ray would pass under it. A part that moved on
  its body is read by ray until still for .3 s, then the body is redrawn; a body past about 45 degrees is read by ray.
  `sample(x, z, hit, low)` passes over a vehicle wholly below `low`.
- `rain-effects.ts`: `createRainSurface` returns `surface.ceiling(rect)`, and with `options.ceiling` a drop is only
  asked where it lands once its streak is down to the highest thing in its 3 m cell. The streaks drawn are identical
  (tested against a run without it). Vehicles are asked apart from that (`options.vehicles`), as they move.
  The ground's ceiling is five samples plus 1 m (`GROUND_RISE`): not a true bound on a cliff inside one cell.
- Cell keys are integers (`rainCell`), and a sample asks for the water once (remembered within the frame in
  `world-atmosphere.ts`).
- Checked: tests (grid against rays on both real models, level and banked; a spinning rotor; a moved part; identical
  streaks), full suite, typecheck. Node benchmark of `atmosphere.update` in Orchard at Ultra, storm minus sun: cockpit
  flying 9.1 -> 1.4 ms, beside a parked helicopter 12.5 -> 2.3 ms, on foot clear of vehicles 3.5 -> 2.0 ms. The engine
  ran it under SwiftShader with no errors and no raycasts in the profile.
- Not checked: the Metal frame times again (the VM's screen was locked, so a new Chrome got no GPU), a tumbling
  wreck, dragon boats. `scripts/vehicle-rain-smoke.mjs` fails on its own stale cap (expects 1,200 drops; the default
  rain detail is High, 5,100): its other assertions hold. `fps-rain-smoke` times out finding `.location-card` at /debug.
  Both untouched here.
- Left: the wet-ground mask (`rain-reflections.ts`) still builds a string key per cell and clears its whole cache at
  24,000 entries, a likely hitch in fast flight; `getProgram` shows about 0.5 ms a frame even in sun.

## Brushed steel bars and bloom fireflies (2026-11-23)

Owner asked for the sun's glint on metal beams (not glass; a per-pane glass tilt trial was shown and dropped).

- `metal-bar.ts`: `roundMetalBars(material)` shades long thin faces of unit-box bars (under 0.6 m across, 3:1 or
  longer) as a rounded, brushed section: the normal swings across the bar, follows the sun's half vector along it, and
  roughness rises with the normal's screen-space change so a bar a pixel or two wide gets a soft sheen instead of
  beads. Works on plain and instanced unit boxes; tubes and plates are untouched. Cache key suffix `round-bars-v3`.
- Marina `steel` and `helixSteel` and Raffles `silver` are also retuned (roughness about .24, metalness .7 to .75,
  envMapIntensity 1.4). The `steel` of the fifteen other districts that have one gets `roundMetalBars` with its
  values unchanged; GPU stills of Orchard, Changi, Tuas and HarbourFront were looked at, the rest were not. Street-prop
  `steel` (bench arms, notice-board posts, tray-return and letterbox frames) has it too; its shader compiled and drew
  on the GPU in Orchard, but no still of a box-built steel prop was captured. `iron` and the districts with no `steel` (Queenstown, Chinatown, Kampong Glam, Little India, Katong, Ubin)
  are untouched.
- `world-occlusion.ts`: the bloom extraction now averages four taps and caps a source pixel at `BLOOM_SOURCE_CAP` (6).
  One unfiltered, unbounded sample turned one-pixel sun highlights into blocky blobs at quarter resolution. This
  touches every bloom source; lamps, muzzle flash and sun on water were not compared before and after.
- The beading and blobs only showed on the real GPU (headless Chrome with Metal); SwiftShader stills looked clean.
  Check highlight changes there before showing them.
- Checked: tests, typecheck, GPU stills of Marina and Raffles in sunny afternoon, SwiftShader stills at night, and the
  owner looked at it live. Not checked: rain, frame rate, the browser smokes, the shader warm-up list.

## Sparks and fragments land on the world (2026-11-23)

Owner asked for particles that interact with the world, "sparks that fall and bounce on the ground", and chose the
CPU version over a GPU simulation (pools are a few hundred particles; no GPU compute exists in the codebase).

- `fps-impacts.ts`: `advanceImpacts(field, dt, ground?)` takes a `GroundLookup` `(x, z, y) => floor | null`. Sparks
  bounce (`SPARK_BOUNCE`) and skitter; hard fragments bounce (`DEBRIS_BOUNCE`), lose their tumble and come to rest
  (`resting`) until they shrink out; leaves and blood drops stay where they land (`bounce: 0`). Each particle remembers
  the floor it last sampled and asks again after 0.25 m of travel; a `null` answer is not remembered, because a spark
  leaving a wall starts inside that wall's footprint. Without `ground` everything behaves as before.
- One surface spark in three (`EMBER_EVERY`) now lives 2.5 times as long (`EMBER_LIFE`, under a second), since the old
  0.2 to 0.4 s lifetimes burnt out before reaching the ground. Target hits keep the short flash. This is a look change.
- `fps-engine.ts`: `particleFloor` is `footMovement.supportHeight(x, z, y, .01, .02)`: terrain, walk surfaces and
  supporting obstacle tops, nothing over open water. Passed to `effects.update` and to `createCombatEventVisuals`
  (`options.ground`), where thrown sparks and chunks re-sample their `floor` each metre instead of bouncing on the
  height the blast went off at.
- Ground only. Nothing collides with walls, vehicles or non-supporting props; a particle that comes down inside such a
  footprint still falls through. Brass still lands on the single `brassFloor` height under the player.
- Checked: tests, typecheck; a throwaway run against the real Marina collision world (about 0.7 microseconds a lookup,
  about 2 lookups a frame under fire, 2253 of 2304 fragments came to rest, the rest fell where there is no support);
  the range entered and fired into the ground in headless Chrome on SwiftShader with no exceptions. Not checked: the
  bounce by eye (SwiftShader ran at about 3 fps), an explosion in the game, frame rate, `pnpm build`, other smokes.
- `scripts/fps-effects-smoke.mjs` is stale since the debug workspace redesign of 2026-11-11: it opens `/debug` and waits
  for a "Marina FPS" button, but the range now sits behind `/debug?tool=fps` and loads straight to "Enter range". Not fixed.

## Aim in the air beats a held sprint (2026-11-24)

Owner asked for scoping in while jumping, "more arcady and call of duty like".

- Nothing gated aim on being grounded; what blocked it was `!sprinting`, and a sprint jump keeps Shift held.
- `fps-engine.ts`: `airAim` latches when aim is held off the ground (not swimming) and clears when aim is released.
  While it is set the sights come up despite the sprint; the jump keeps its sprint speed in the air, and after the
  landing the held aim drops the run to aimed pace until aim is let go.
- Follow-up the same day, owner's call: aim beats sprint on the ground too. A held aim goes into
  `advanceSprintBreak` as the trigger does, so the run drops and the sights wait out `burden.sprintOut`
  (`sightsReady`). Sights already up skip the raise, so a landing or a shot from an aimed jump does not wait.
  `airAim` is no longer a latch: in the air the sprint speed is kept, on the ground the aim breaks it.
- Toggled aim (Q, touch button): a fresh sprint-key press that asks for a sprint drops it
  (`sprintDropsToggledAim` in `fps-sprint.ts`). The touch stick at the rim does not, and the autopilot is exempt.
- A grenade in hand is exempt: aim there is the lob and does not break the run.
- Not changed: airborne spread and recoil penalties.
- Checked: tests, typecheck. Not checked in a browser.
